detail_description:
What better way to enjoy a Perth summer day than playing on the beautiful Swan River?
9:00am - 5:00pm
Even if you have never sailed or paddled before, Funcat's friendly and experienced staff will have you out on the water in no time. After some basic tuition and demonstration, you will be out sailing on the beautiful swan river before you know it. Our Hobie cats up to four people, so those nobody will miss out on any of the fun. For the more experienced sailor you may enjoy the perfect racing arena that is found on the Swan.
detail_booking_notes:
To help ensure a great day out we ask you and your guests and family to please be mindful of the following:

Everyone sailing needs to be prepared to get wet! Even in light winds water will sweep across the decks, so you will likely be wet from, at least the waist down. Also be aware that it is always cooler on the water, so wearing a spray jacket or warm top on the catamarans isn't such a bad idea. It's also a good idea to bring a change of clothes, if you are planning on staying at the river after your sail

In the past we have had some issues with theft from cars in the car park behind Funcats, so we strongly recommend you do not leave valuable is your car. If you have nobody ashore to look after your valuables, we would be happy to do so for you.

Please keep it in mind that we often see back-to-back bookings with our catamarans, so we do ask that you and your guests and family are ready to head out on the water at least 15-20 minutes prior to your booked time. This gives us enough time to be able to kit everyone out with life jackets and take you through a lesson (if required) and safety briefing.
We want you to be able to enjoy the full hour, or two, you have booked and this is the best way to ensure this happens.
detail_restrictions:
Q. At what age is it safe to take children on a catamaran?
A. 5 years of age is the youngest age we will allow children on the catamarans. If you wish to take young children on a catamaran, we suggest that you discuss this with us on the day. Factors such as sailing experience of the person in charge of the catamaran and the conditions on the day very much influence the advice we give to hirers.
Someone 16 or over MUST be present on each boat in your hire. If you do not have a 16-year-old or older present, unfortunately your booking will be forfeit.

Customers will also receive a full refund or credit in case of operator cancellation due to weather or other unforeseen circumstances. Contact us by phone to cancel or inquire about a cancellation. No-shows will be charged the full price.

Your coach will introduce themselves and gets you sorted with a wetsuit and board.
You will start with some beach-based technique and surf safety info. We are big on getting it right on the beach and getting you ready to hit the waves.

Surf coaches will help get you up and riding by pushing you into a few waves, giving feedback on your technique, keeping an eye on your safety, encouraging you and maximising your fun.

detail_description:
Adults High Performance Coaching program is for any Adult who can independently paddle out the back and trim across an unbroken wave. Our program runs for 2 days:

Our high performance coaching camps are about reaching your true surfing ability with the help of a few clever strategies, delivered by our highly qualified, professional and friendly coaches.

Video Analysis: We use video analysis to improve your surfing technique and skill level. Our high performance coaches film your surfing session from the beach, then sit with you to go over your footage in detail and give you constructive feedback on your strengths and areas in need of improvement. detail_description:
Monkey Mia Marine Life Cruise 2 – 1:30 PM to 3:30 PM
This cruise is offered only during the Western Australia School Holidays and opens for booking once our Morning Cruise (10:00 AM – 12:30 PM) is nearing capacity. A minimum of 10 adults is required to operate this cruise.
Step aboard the spectacular 18-metre sailing catamaran, Aristocat 2, for a cruise through nature’s aquarium in search of dugongs, sponging dolphins, loggerhead and green turtles, manta rays, and other amazing and endangered marine life. The experience also includes an energising salt spa in the boom net, with multiple vantage points to enjoy the stunning surroundings.
We are the only cruise operator licensed to interact with marine life in the Exclusion Zone. This means as soon as we leave the jetty, we can stop at any time to take full advantage of your marine life sighting experience. We will go in search of marine life including dolphins, dugongs, turtles, rays, and sharks from the moment we leave the jetty.
Boom netting is available on this cruise.
Viewing vantage points around the entire boat
All-weather outdoor & indoor seating
Boom net (bring your bathers and towel)
Indoor fully licensed Ocean Lounge Bar
Wheelchair access throughout the boat
Wheelchair-accessible toilet
While we strive to spot wild animals on our Marine Life Cruises, sightings cannot be guaranteed. Our skipper and crew have many years of experience in Shark Bay and will always do their best to find animals for you to observe. Sightings may vary seasonally; dugong season runs from August to May.
detail_important_info:
Cruise Information: Please meet at the Monkey Mia Jetty 15 minutes prior to departure for your Monkey Mia Marine Life Cruise
Monkey Mia is 25 kilometres from the town of Denham, about a 20 minute drive.
Passenger Information: Drinks and snacks are available for purchase on board including beer, wine, champagne, soft drinks, juice, tea, coffee & water, chips and muesli bars. We also allow BYO drinks and snacks.
Weather Information: All activities and cruises are subject to weather conditions and at the skipper’s discretion.
Please remember, we cannot control the weather. We still run cruises on windy, overcast and rainy days. We always advise to check the weather before your cruise date.
detail_booking_notes: Marine Life Experience: As we endeavour to look at wild animals while on our Marine Life Cruises there is no guarantee that we will sight animals during the cruise. The skipper and crew have many years of experience in Shark Bay and will always try their hardest to find animals for you to look at. Unfortunately due to seasonal changes our sightings will vary. Dugong season is August - May. Dugong sightings are more challenging in winter months

detail_important_info:
Important Information:
Medical info:
While certified divers are required to fill out the medical form on-board as well, their certification status allows them a bit more leeway in determining their medical fitness to dive. Certified divers (divers with a licence) generally need to be able to answer the following questions:
Since completing your last dive medical assessment, have you suffered any illness or injury that may affect your ability to dive safely?
Are you currently suffering any illness or injury?
Are you currently taking any prescription medication, other than the contraceptive pill?
Certified divers are generally allowed to dive if they can answer “no” to the first two questions. If they are taking prescription medication, they are generally okay to dive if they were taking it while they were doing their course or have had an updated medical.
Example if you have not dived for a few years and you are taking medication (especially if it is for anxiety, high blood pressure or anything else relating to heart /lungs) you would not be able to scuba dive in Queensland until a dive doctor has put in writing FIT TO DIVE.
We cannot refund if it turns out on the dive day that you suffer from a condition incompatible with diving and you fail to bring a clear to dive confirmation from an accredited dive doctor.
View Australian Dive Doctors.pdf (https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/frW9Ab8aTwyWWpB0f1Zz)
What to bring:
A towel, sunglasses, hat, swimmers and a change of clothes, dive log book and your certification card (if you are a certified diver).
Sunscreen:
Sunscreen is found to be damaging the reef, coral are very sensitive to chemical additives found in conventional sunscreen, which is why we recommend you to cover yourself with clothes. However, Reef and skin friendly sunscreen with no harmful additives is available at our shop.
Keep Warm & Protected:
If you suffer from the cold or prefer to have your own personal under garment, we have a variety at our shop. We provide: Good humour and all snorkel/dive equipment, lycra (stinger/rash guard suits) or wet suits, buffet lunch, tea/coffee, fruit and cakes & water.
Seasickness?
If you are not sure prevention is better than cure.
We recommend TRAVACALM (Pink&white box), a non drowsy medication available at most chemists in Australia. Take medication 1 hour before boat departure (otherwise medication won’t work). Please read more about it here. (https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/1mPlz4jR0ajaS6pfIaXu)

detail_important_info: IMPORTANT THINGS YOU NEED TO KNOW...
detail_booking_notes:
Cellar Doors:
Your day is your own where you have the freedom to pick and choose who you want to visit 
but don't worry about doing too much planning in advance as we will be here to help you on the day with lots of up-to-date information about the cellar doors, as well as heaps of friendly advice about how you can make the most of your day, too. 😊

There are upwards of 14+ beautiful cellar doors who are more than happy for you to visit them for a tasting without the need to book an appointment in advance, however, there are some exceptions to this rule:-
Cloudy Bay: (a 40 minute bike ride from our base)
Hunters: (a 40 minute bike ride from our base)
Hans Herzog: (a 20 minute bike ride from our base)
Framingham Wines: (a 10 minute bike ride from our base)

If any of these 4 cellar doors are on your bucket list, just head to their websites to find their booking forms. With Cloudy Bay and Hunters being 40 minutes away, we would recommend you make a booking between 12 Noon -1pm so that you get the big bike ride out of the way at the start of the day when you are nice and fresh, then you can work your way back and be close to home at the end of the day. 😊 

There are some cellar doors that we feel are too far away to get to on a bike, or that the roads to reach them are just not safe - Clos Henri, Saint Clair's, Wither Hills, Lawsons Dry Hills - we feel these are best visited by car.

For groups over 8+ pax - the cellar doors do ask that we book you in and we will work with you and help put together a personalized itinerary and get spots secured at the cellar doors for you.

Cheese & Mixed Platters:
Most of the cellar doors have platter food available for purchase if you wish to have something to nibble on alongside your tastings. These can be ordered when you arrive at the cellar door.

Restaurants:
Bookings are recommended and we are always here to help if you are not sure what time to book😊
Vines Village Café: 20 minutes biking from our base (Open 7 days a week).
The Fancy Cow: 25 minutes biking from our base (Open 6 days, closed on Mondays)
Allan Scott: 40 minutes biking from our base – bookings essential - (Open 7 days a week)
Number 11 at Wairau River: 15 minutes biking from our base - (Open 7 days a week as of 7th November 2024)

Note: Wither Hills and Saint Clair’s restaurants are not accessible on our bikes - they are too far away and the roads are not safe getting to them - we feel they are best visited by car :-)

For those on the Roadsters:
These bikes need to stay on the bike paths and quiet roads, so the beautiful cellar doors you can visit are...
Gibson Bridge
Forrest Wines: - platters available for purchase
Framingham Wines: - "build your own platter" - food available for purchase
Nautilus Estate: - platter food available for purchase
Bladen: - food truck & platters food available for purchase (closed on Wednesdays)
Boomtown Beer Garden: - food truck (Open Thurs-Sun as of 1st November 2024)
Number 11 at Wairau River: - restaurant and tasting room (Open 7 days a week as of 7th November 2024)

We are really looking forward to seeing you but if you have any questions before you arrive, please just ask away as we are always here to help :-)

Calling using an International Phone - (+64) 3 572 7954 or (+64) 27 249 5646

**Our Cancellation Policy**

We value the booking you make with us and will guarantee that your bikes are secured for you when we confirm.  Please remember, keeping your bikes aside means that no-one else can book them, so cancellations have a big effect on our small family business.

Before transporting any individual to the Tongariro Alpine Crossing, it is mandatory for all passengers to verify possession of a confirmed booking issued by the Department of Conservation for access to the Tongariro Alpine Crossing.
Upon arrival at the car park please ensure you have your booking reference of your shuttle and either a paper or electronic copy of your confirmed booking from the Department of Conservation readily available.
Please board any departing shuttle from this location to reach the trek's starting point.
The journey from the Private Car Park to the Mangatepopo trailhead covers 20 km and typically takes approximately 35 minutes.
National Park Shuttles is the sole Tangata Whenua (local people) operator based in Waimarino National Park Village, providing reliable transportation from the only all-day car park to the Tongariro Alpine Crossing. The secure parking facility is on State Highway 46, 400 meters from the road-end entrance to the Ketetahi track.
MAP: https://maps.app.goo.gl/j5HeiQwmQMcRo7Tn7
Be prepared for unexpected weather conditions. Weather-appropriate clothing and footwear are essential for your journey, including garments suitable for warmth, wet conditions, and wind.
Ensure that your mobile phone is sufficiently charged and include a head torch in your packing list.
This demanding journey commences at 1,120 metres ascending through Mangatepopo Valley to the saddle between Mount Tongariro and Mount Ngauruhoe. The route passes through South Crater before ascending once more to Red Crater, the highest point on the crossing at 1,886 metres.
Following this you will descend via a volcanic rock scree track to the Emerald Lakes (Ngarotopounamu), noted for their distinctive greenstone hue. After walking past Blue Lake also known as Te Wai-whakaata-o-te-Rangihiroa (Rangihiroa’s mirror), the track skirts the northern slopes of Tongariro eventually descending in a zigzag fashion to the road terminus at 760 metres.
Collection is provided from the private car park which features security cameras and is staffed by security personnel.
Roadside parking along the main highway is not recommended due to safety and security concerns.
The journey to the start of the Tongariro Alpine Crossing is tranquil and comfortable.
We prioritise customer safety throughout the experience.
Upon completion of the trek please note there is an additional 950-metre walk returning to the car park where your vehicle is located.
We want your experience with us to be wonderful. Traveling with our trusted Manawhenua shuttle partners means you can enjoy a smooth and reliable trip, and we genuinely appreciate your patience along the way. Thank you for supporting our local businesses.

product_headline: Ages 13+ • 5 hours • SUP & Snorkel morning adventure on the Mornington Peninsula including breakfast
detail_description:
Its impossible to regret getting up early and heading into nature especially in Australia with the abundance of wildlife active at that time. Doesn't get much better on this day of paddleboarding & snorkelling adventure on the most majestic waterways of the Mornington Peninsula.
An incredible day of eco-adventure in stunning Aussie nature of the Mornington Peninsula where you will feel a world away.
Join us on a SUP & snorkel expedition to two unique waterways off the beaten track.
Explore a beautiful inland waterway keeping an eye out for kangaroos, eagles and turtles, stopping for a floating morning tea along the way. Back on land it's time to enjoy a lakeside brunch full of fresh local produce. Full SUP lesson and tour included from our qualified guides. After brunch we head to a special ocean location to paddle & snorkel the crystal clear waters along the Peninsula's incredible coastline.
The day includes SUP lesson and tour, guided ocean snorkelling experience, awesome brunch, floating morning tea, complimentary refreshments and return transport to your Mornington Peninsula accommodation (return transport from Melbourne accommodation can be arranged at an additional cost)
detail_booking_notes:
Thanks for choosing your adventure with WAM! We can't wait for you to join us on a spectacular journey into nature.

Just by booking with us, you have done a lot of good for the planet, congratulations! (read on for more details of how)

Before we do so, please take a minute to read some important information about your tour:

WAM Adventures require a minimum of 4 people to run. We almost always run our trips but we'll be in contact as we get closer to the date for updates.
You’ll start receiving emails as we get closer to the date.
Once you have a date confirmed, if you need to cancel, we require a minimum 7 days notice to provide a refund (please read our T&C's for other options)

Gift vouchers: If you have a gift voucher, you'll need to redeem it at some stage by returning to the relevant tour page, selecting a date and entering the voucher code at the checkout - think of your voucher as like a pre-paid credit card
Also, we can’t extend the use-by date on gift vouchers past three years (three years is pretty good!)

Premium Service: We include everything you need on your adventure including activities, equipment, food and refreshments.
To maximise your comfort we even provide you with eco-pack for the day which includes some special products from local businesses that directly support the environment. This includes free sunscreen and a towel service. You simply hand these back at the end of your experience. Its a bit like a pack you may get on a first class flight or a luxury hotel, except ours is good for the planet!

Now for the deep and meaningful:
By booking an adventure with us you have directly helped make a long-term positive environmental and social impact by:
Planting native trees on the Mornington Peninsula with MP Koalas to capture carbon emissions, protect our climate, enhance soil and water quality, and restore habitat for native wildlife.
Regenerate reefs and native kelp locally with The Nature Conservancy, providing marine habitat, filtering seawater, removing nitrogen and phosphate, and preventing used shell from entering landfill.
Support female education with The Stars Foundation which empowers and supports Indigenous young women and girls to complete education and find work.
Protect and plant mangroves to protect our coastlines, wildlife and support blue carbon projects.

You'll find additional information relevant to your adventure on the Wild Adventures Melbourne website. Please check the website for exactly what items we recommend bringing with you on the day.

Green is our Gold Commitment:
As members of Australia’s tourism industry, we believe a land as precious
as ours should be preserved for generations to come. As a visitor, we ask that you do the same. That’s why we’ve set some unwritten rules that have kept our backyard beautiful for thousands of years.

Passed down through story and practice, they’re how we walk gently, listen deeply, tread with care – and look out for each other along the way.

By following them throughout your visit, you too can care for Australia when you Come and say G’day.

Consider these principles a bit of local knowledge. A few fundamentals to help you respect this place and have an unforgettable stay in the process.

The Guiding Principles:
Celebrate Community: The best part of an Australian visit is the people you meet.
Shop local, engage with communities, and you’ll leave with new mates aplenty.

Embrace Culture: Australia’s cultural diversity stretches from ancient songlines to city laneways. Immerse yourself in it all - honour First Nations cultures, embrace our diversity, and you’ll leave with new knowledge and new friends.

Preserve Place: In Australia you’ll find some of the most unspoilt landscapes on Earth. Help keep them that way by minimising your impact wherever you go.

Respect Wildlife: Australia has some of the most unique animals on the planet. Take as many photos as you like but remember to give them space and respect their homes.

Take Care: We look out for one another in Australia, but it’s important to take care of yourself too. Listen to the land, respect it, and always put safety first.

If you have any questions between now and your trip with us, please don't hesitate to email or call me directly.
detail_meeting_point: Pick up Location: We meet on the Mornington Peninsula at Devilbend Natural Features Reserve, 159 Graydens Rd, Moorooduc VIC 3933. Please contact us if you would like to discuss an alternative pick up location on the Mornington Peninsula, or we can also pick up from Frankston Train Station.
detail_what_to_bring: Please bring hat, swimwear, sunglasses, camera, comfortable clothes suitable for the activities and weather (including warmer clothes and rainjacket), sandals/flips flops/jandals/thongs), change of clothes for the trip back.
detail_health_safety: Participants must be able to swim. Life jackets are available if required.
detail_cancellation_policy:
VARIATIONS AND CANCELLATIONS
WAM is committed to providing its customers (you) with an enjoyable and safe trip. Trips can occasionally be affected by weather, and other unforeseen factors outside of our control (including adverse weather conditions, or an insufficient number of passengers for us to run the trip) may require us to alter routes, itineraries, fares, days of operation or even cancel tours. We retain the right to do any of these things without notice (however, where practical we will endeavour to provide you with notice of alterations or cancellations). We require a minimum of 4 passengers to run a trip and have a maximum of 8 passengers. If we need to cancel a trip due to there being less than 4 passengers, we will endeavour to provide you with at least 12 hours’ notice of such cancellation.

In the event of unforeseen circumstances such as extreme weather, we may be unable to operate the tour on a specific day. In this case, you will be offered an alternative date. If however you are not able to attend a trip on a different date, we will provide you with a full refund. To the extent permitted by law, no refunds will be provided due to alterations to any aspect of the trip.
If you cancel a trip booking at least 7 days in advance of the trip, we will provide you with your choice of a refund of any trip fares already paid, or a credit note for a future trip. No refund will be provided for cancellations within 7 days of the trip date, however we will allow you to transfer that trip booking into another person’s name. A $25 administrative fee will apply to all booking changes within 7 days of departure.

Cancellations made more than 48 hours prior to the scheduled hire, tour, or shuttle will receive a full refund.
Cancellations made within 48 hours of the scheduled hire, tour, or shuttle for services provided directly by Riverside Adventures Waikato are non-refundable.

Bike, kayak and SUP hire, shuttle services, and guided bike and kayak tours operate in most weather conditions. Weather-related changes do not automatically qualify for a refund. Where possible, we are happy to offer rescheduling to an alternative date (subject to availability).

detail_booking_notes:
Please arrive 20 minutes prior to your booking to allow you enough time to sign in. However we recommend you sign in prior to arriving via the online pre-arrival waiver. You should receive an email "action required" from "wherewolf" at the time you made your booking. This will save you time when you get here.
For Boat, Kayak and SUP hire only the group leader or captain needs to sign in..........

Please ensure to arrive early so you don't miss out on "your" boating time. More often than not your boat has a booking straight after so it's not always possible for us to extend your hire time. If we can we will.
Make sure your whole group is present and ready 20 minutes BEFORE your booking time
Regardless of this send the Captain to the office to get checked in and receive a boat briefing/induction. If you're late send the captain to us asap.

The Driver/Captain of the boat must be physically checking in at our office 15-20 minutes BEFORE your booking time to ensure you receive the full duration of your hire time
(if you are running late, this may impact your total hire time, as you are due to return according to your booking time. This is due to the boat being booked out one after the other)
If you have lots of gear to bring, we suggest the group brings this down while the Captain is getting their induction. This process usually takes 15 mins so your group does not need to panic.

All bookings have a safety briefing which begins at the time of your hire or just before if you're early. Late arrivals are not automatically subject to additional hire time. Safety briefings can take approximately 10-15 minutes

Cafe On-Site: Raffertys Cafe is operating on-site here.

If you have any questions, please feel free to give us a call!

Coming from out of town? If joining us at Lake Macquarie, we are located at Raffertys Resort which has plenty of accommodation to suit your needs.

Please note this booking is subject to weather
Please note Dogs are not allowed in the Resort or on our hire boats

product_headline: 3 consecutive day beginner surf  program (5 -14yrs)
detail_description:
Beginner Surfing Program with all equipment!
Over three consecutive fun filled days, you learn all the key base skills for paddling correctly and getting to your feet and riding with a good technique. You also get a thorough rundown of surf safety, ocean awareness, and surfing rules. You will progress your surfing with a focus on catching more waves, getting to your feet efficiently, surfing with the correct stance, and riding waves consistently. You will now be more confident in the surf and improving well.
The more lessons you surf with us, the more surfing skills and knowledge you will have to get past that initial, frustrating beginner stage.
Our instructors are there to help you learn to surf and provide advice on all questions related to surfing. We hope that you’ll love surfing as much as we do. We'll get you up and riding in no time!
Roll up at the beach at your start time with your swimwear on.
Your coach will introduce themselves and gets you sorted with a wetsuit and board.
You will start with some beach-based technique and surf safety info. We are big on getting it right on the beach and getting you ready to hit the waves.
You then hit the surf in waist deep water and waves suitable for your ability.
Surf coaches will help get you up and riding by pushing you into a few waves, giving feedback on your technique, keeping an eye on your safety, encouraging you and maximising your fun.
Surfers will leave the water approximately 15mins prior to the end of the lesson.
A feedback session with goals for your next surf lesson is done before getting changed.

Our equipment is the best available on the market and produced specifically for surf schools. We use soft, stable boards that are easy to balance, paddle, stand and surf on for intermediate and beginner surfers. Presented as a special experience, the cruise suits families and groups seeking a scenic, secluded outing.
detail_booking_notes:
Hooray! Your booking is confirmed.

We are happy to inform you that your booking for our Western Bays Adventurer is confirmed!

A local snorkelling experience
Have an experienced dive professional help you understand the local environment so you can better enjoy the snorkel adventure.
Your guide will brief you on the site, conditions and points of interest, plus describe the aquatic life you’ll see and how to interact with local creatures responsibly.
Snorkelling with an experienced local lets you relax. They will show you what to do to make your dive fun and hassle free. The location will be selected on the day for the best conditions.

detail_booking_notes:
Thank you for booking a snorkel tour with us. We're really looking forward to taking you out and showing you why this coastline is such a special place to explore.

Depending on the conditions on the day, you might encounter some of our local favourites — cryptic nudibranchs, seahorses, and the lively kelp gardens that shelter Eden’s weedy sea dragons and curious wrasse.

It’s also common to see rays gliding along the sand, schools of fish, and the occasional octopus tucked into a rocky hideout. If we're lucky, we may even meet a friendly blue grouper or hear whales singing in the distance during migration season.

Below is some additional information to help you prepare for your tour, including forms to complete.
Sites are weather-dependent and usually 5–25 minutes away
If you have any questions, please let me know.
diveeden@gmail.com (mailto:diveeden@gmail.com)

Enthusiasm and a sense of adventure

detail_disclaimers:
Milford Sound Risk Disclosure: Visitors to Milford Sound should be aware of various natural hazards when going to Milford Sound.
Aotearoa New Zealand: Powerful natural forces have shaped Aotearoa New Zealand over millions of years. Earthquakes and volcanoes lifted these beautiful islands out of the Pacific Ocean. They have created the dramatic landscapes we enjoy today.
Natural hazards are part of life here. Around 20,000 earthquakes are recorded each year. Most are small and go unnoticed, but larger events can cause damage. Understanding the hazards and how to stay safe is an important part of planning your visit.
Piopiotahi Milford Sound: Dramatic and ever-changing, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is one of the world’s most spectacular and special environments. Its steep, glacier-carved mountains and deep fiord have been shaped by powerful geological forces over millions of years.
The area is exposed to risk from a range of natural hazards. These can occur at any time, and some can happen without warning. Of all the hazards, large earthquakes, landslides and tsunamis pose the greatest risk to people at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
It is extremely unlikely that one will happen during your visit, especially for a short stay. However, there is a risk and the longer you spend there, the higher it becomes. Once you are there, your safety options are limited and it is important you understand the risks, before you go.
Earthquakes at Piopiotahi Milford Sound: Like the rest of Aotearoa New Zealand, small earthquakes occur regularly in Fiordland. We don’t feel them and they don’t bother us. These small movements are a normal part of how the land works and do not pose a risk to people.
Sometimes, earthquakes in or near Fiordland are felt at Piopiotahi Milford Sound. They might shake objects on a shelf or rattle a window, but they do not cause major impacts or disrupt your visit.
Occasionally, a stronger earthquake can trigger avalanches, rockfall or landslides. These can cause debris to fall onto roads, jetties and tracks, and may disrupt your travel plans if you happen to be nearby.
Large earthquakes are rare, and extremely unlikely to happen during a short visit. But they will happen again.
The Alpine Fault runs almost the entire length of the South Island and crosses the entrance to Piopiotahi Milford Sound. It can generate earthquakes of magnitude 8 or greater, occurring on average every 300 years. There is a 75% chance of this happening in the next 50 years (find out more at af8.org.nz) (https://af8.org.nz/). An earthquake of this size would almost certainly affect the narrow waterway and surrounding area.
What to do in an earthquake: DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries from earthquakes happen when you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the ground/floor you are, the less likely you are to be injured.
Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
For more detailed information, please visit Emergency Management Southland (https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or AF8 (https://af8.org.nz/).

What to do in an earthquake:
DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries from earthquakes happen when you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the ground/floor you are, the less likely you are to be injured.
Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
For more detailed information, please visit Emergency Management Southland (https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or AF8 (https://af8.org.nz/).

detail_description:
Join us for an awesome winter adventure with bucket loads of wildlife, relaxation, active adventure and local produce.
Your adventure starts with pick up from Melbourne CBD accommodation or your Mornington Peninsula accommodation, from here your WAM guide takes you to Westernport Bay to remarkable whale watching cruise with Wildlife Coast Cruises along the spectacular Peninsula coastline spotting humpback whales or southern right whales making their annual migration.
Following the cruise, we’ll take you on a short drive to a fantastic ocean viewpoint location for a warming winter lunch full of fresh local produce.
Refueled from lunch, we head to the balcony of the southern ocean, for a short coastal hike before making our way to the Peninsula Hot Springs, or Alba Thermal Springs for heavenly bathing experiences immersed in nature including hot pools, saunas and steam rooms.
Feeling refreshed, relaxed and warmed up, we’ll head back to the vehicle and return to Melbourne early evening to say farewell after a beautiful winter adventure.
detail_booking_notes:
Just by booking with us, you have done a lot of good for the planet, congratulations! (read on for more details of how)
Before we do so, please take a minute to read some important information about your tour:
WAM Adventures require a minimum of 4 people to run. We almost always run our trips but we'll be in contact as we get closer to the date for updates.
You’ll start receiving emails as we get closer to the date.
Once you have a date confirmed, if you need to cancel, we require a minimum 7 days notice to provide a refund (please read our T&C's for other options)
Gift vouchers: If you have a gift voucher, you'll need to redeem it at some stage by returning to the relevant tour page, selecting a date and entering the voucher code at the checkout - think of your voucher as like a pre-paid credit card
Also, we can’t extend the use-by date on gift vouchers past three years (three years is pretty good!)
Premium Service:
We include everything you need on your adventure including activities, equipment, food and refreshments.
To maximise your comfort we even provide you with eco-pack for the day which includes some special gifts and products from local businesses that directly support the environment. This includes free sunscreen and a towel service. You simply hand these back at the end of your experience. Its a bit like a pack you may get on a first class flight or a luxury hotel, except ours is good for the planet!
Now for the deep and meaningful:
By booking an adventure with us you have directly helped make a long-term positive environmental and social impact by:
Planting native trees on the Mornington Peninsula with MP Koalas to capture carbon emissions, protect our climate, enhance soil and water quality, and restore habitat for native wildlife.
Regenerate reefs and native kelp locally with The Nature Conservancy, providing marine habitat, filtering seawater, removing nitrogen and phosphate, and preventing used shell from entering landfill.
Support female education with The Stars Foundation which empowers and supports Indigenous young women and girls to complete education and find work.
Protect and plant mangroves to protect our coastlines, wildlife and support blue carbon projects.
You'll find additional information relevant to your adventure on the Wild Adventures Melbourne website. Please check the website for exactly what items we recommend bringing with you on the day.
Green is our Gold Commitment:
As members of Australia’s tourism industry, we believe a land as precious
as ours should be preserved for generations to come. As a visitor, we ask that you do the same. That’s why we’ve set some unwritten rules that have kept our backyard beautiful for thousands of years.
Passed down through story and practice, they’re how we walk gently, listen deeply, tread with care – and look out for each other along the way.
By following them throughout your visit, you too can care for Australia when you Come and say G’day.
Consider these principles a bit of local knowledge. A few fundamentals to help you respect this place and have an unforgettable stay in the process.
The Guiding Principles:
Celebrate Community
The best part of an Australian visit is the people you meet.
Shop local, engage with communities, and you’ll leave with new mates aplenty.
Embrace Culture
Australia’s cultural diversity stretches from ancient songlines to city laneways. Immerse yourself in it all - honour First Nations cultures, embrace our diversity, and you’ll leave with new knowledge and new friends.
Preserve Place
In Australia you’ll find some of the most unspoilt landscapes on Earth. Help keep them that way by minimising your impact wherever you go.
Respect Wildlife
Australia has some of the most unique animals on the planet. Take as many photos as you like but remember to give them space and respect their homes.
Take Care
We look out for one another in Australia, but it’s important to take care of yourself too. Listen to the land, respect it, and always put safety first.
If you have any questions between now and your trip with us, please don't hesitate to email or call me directly.

detail_booking_notes:
Precis of Queensland cycling rules and safety:
RULES:
PATHWAYS:
Shared pathways:
Keep Left, ring bell to warn of passing pedestrians
Cyclists give way to people, slow down
Separate pathways:
Cyclists use the side of the pathway indicated by the sign
Bicycle only:
For bicycles only
You can use any speed
On-road bicycle lanes:
You must follow all road rules
You are sharing the road with other vehicles
Keep as far left as possible
NO Bicycle zone:
You must dismount and walk your bike
DO NOT RIDE IN PUBLIC SQUARES, WALK YOUR BIKE.
RIDING:
Keep at two hands on handlebars unless giving signals.
Have one leg on each side of the seat.
Face forward.
To signal RIGHT-TURN, extend arm out horizontally with hand open, palm facing forward. To signal STOP, raise arm with elbow bent at right angle and hand up with palm facing forward.
One person per bike unless the bike is designed as a tandem bike.
Keep two meters from the back of a vehicle when following.
DO NOT ride into the path of a driver or pedestrian.
Keep left at all times.
Do not overtake another vehicle on the left if that vehicle is indicating and turning left.
Do not ride more than two abreast.
If riding beside another rider, ride no more than 1.5m apart.
For a more comprehensive list of rules go to https://www.qld.gov.au/transport/safety/rules/wheeled-devices/bicycle
IF YOU BREAK THE ROAD RULES YOU MAY BE FINED. THERE IS NO AGE LIMIT FOR BEING FINED.
SAFETY:
Wear your helmet and enclosed shoes
Cycle at appropriate speed.
Go slow when there are people about.
Ring the bell when approaching pedestrians, dogs, etc.
Keep left at all times.
Use appropriate lights and reflectors in low light level situations and at night.

detail_description:
Have you ever wanted to snorkel with manta rays and experience the breathtaking Ningaloo Reef?
This full day tour takes you around to the most spectacular locations! We take both divers and snorkelers together on board this day tour!
Experience the unique opportunity to snorkel up close with our resident population of these amazing creatures, Manta Rays, and SCUBA dive or snorkel the world heritage listed Ningaloo Reef!!
The full day tour meets at 8:00am and returns between 14:30 and 15:30. We start by checking you in at our shop (Shop 8, Coral Bay Arcade) where we will provide you with all the equipment you need for the day. Then, we head down to the jetty on our buses to begin the days adventure!
This tour includes 2 dives or 2 snorkels on the incredible Ningaloo reef. Here, you will have the opportunity to see a variety of tropical fish, possibly turtles, sharks and definitely beautiful coral structures. In between the 2 dives/snorkels we head out into Batemans Bay, a sandy bottom bay and send our spotter plane out in search for manta rays. If we are successful in locating manta rays, you will then you will have the opportunity to snorkel with them.
Once we have completed our manta ray interaction portion of the day we will cruise around the bay in search of other marine animals while the crew prepare lunch. We provide a buffet style lunch on board and can accommodate for any dietary requirements. Once we have filled our bellies, we head back over to the Ningaloo reef and enter the water for our final in water activity! We then head back to the jetty and finish the day back at the shop.
Our dive sites are beautiful coral reef dives that have a varied depth of 4m to 12m with our average depth being at 6-8m. As the Ningaloo Reef is a fringing reef, it is quite shallow all around but filled with spectacular coral structures and marine life. All of our dives are guided dives with maximum group sizes of 8, although we typically have smaller groups.
Our dives are 45-50 minutes long and the average visibility in Coral Bay is 10-15m but can vary depending on conditions. The water temperature varies from 20C up to 26C in the summer and we provide full length 5mm wetsuits for all divers.
detail_important_info: SEASONAL.CONSIDERATIONS: November to April can also bring unpredictable weather conditions, including cyclones. If you’re planning to visit the Ningaloo Reef during this period, we recommend keeping these seasonal factors in mind and allowing flexibility in your travel plans.
detail_booking_notes:
Please keep in mind that our dealings with wild animals in their natural environment are unpredictable. Our commitment to you is that our crew will make every possible effort to ensure that you have the best experience possible, however we cannot guarantee that we will see all or any of the wildlife mentioned. There is no refund if we are unable to locate the wildlife on your specific day.
We can only take children old enough to walk and move around unaided as we have dive equipment on board and a parent/guardian must be with them at all times throughout the duration of the tour.
We are a “reef safe sunscreen” operation. Reef safe sunscreen is available for our customers both in-store and on our vessel. We also have full length wetsuits available to reduce the overuse of sunscreen on our tours. We encourage guests to only bring reef safe sunscreen on our vessel.
We provide reusable cups on tour, but you’re welcome to bring your own reusable water bottle or coffee cup to help us reduce waste and protect the environment.

Ready for an Adventure of the body, mind and tastebuds?

detail_booking_notes:
Just by booking with us, you have done a lot of good for the planet, congratulations! (read on for more details of how)

Before we do so, please take a minute to read some important information about your tour:
- If you need to cancel, we require a minimum 7 days notice to provide a refund (please read our T&C's for other options)
Please check in and sign the waiver prior to the date of your adventure.
We also provide you with an insulated picnic backpack, with picnic mat and everything else you need for the perfect day out. Please return this along with any equipment at the end of your adventure.

Gift vouchers: If you have a gift voucher, you'll need to redeem it at some stage by returning to the relevant tour page, selecting a date and entering the voucher code at the checkout - think of your voucher as like a pre-paid credit card
Also, we can’t extend the use-by date on gift vouchers past three years (three years is pretty good!)

Now for the deep and meaningful:
By booking an adventure with us you have directly helped make a long-term positive environmental and social impact by:
- Planting native trees on the Mornington Peninsula with MP Koalas to capture carbon emissions, protect our climate, enhance soil and water quality, and restore habitat for native wildlife.
- Regenerate reefs and native kelp locally with The Nature Conservancy, providing marine habitat, filtering seawater, removing nitrogen and phosphate, and preventing used shell from entering landfill.
- Support female education with The Stars Foundation which empowers and supports Indigenous young women and girls to complete education and find work.
- Protect and plant mangroves to protect our coastlines, wildlife and support blue carbon projects.

You'll find additional information relevant to your adventure on the Wild Adventures Melbourne website. Please check the website for exactly what items we recommend bringing with you on the day.

Green is our Gold Commitment:

As members of Australia’s tourism industry, we believe a land as precious
as ours should be preserved for generations to come. As a visitor, we ask that you do the same. That’s why we’ve set some unwritten rules that have kept our backyard beautiful for thousands of years.

Passed down through story and practice, they’re how we walk gently, listen deeply, tread with care – and look out for each other along the way. 

By following them throughout your visit, you too can care for Australia when you Come and say G’day.

Consider these principles a bit of local knowledge. A few fundamentals to help you respect this place and have an unforgettable stay in the process.

The Guiding Principles:

Celebrate Community: The best part of an Australian visit is the people you meet.
Shop local, engage with communities, and you’ll leave with new mates aplenty.

Embrace Culture: Australia’s cultural diversity stretches from ancient songlines to city laneways. Immerse yourself in it all - honour First Nations cultures, embrace our diversity, and you’ll leave with new knowledge and new friends.

Preserve Place: In Australia you’ll find some of the most unspoilt landscapes on Earth. Help keep them that way by minimising your impact wherever you go.

Respect Wildlife: Australia has some of the most unique animals on the planet. Take as many photos as you like but remember to give them space and respect their homes.

Take Care: We look out for one another in Australia, but it’s important to take care of yourself too. Listen to the land, respect it, and always put safety first.

If you have any questions between now and your trip with us, please don't hesitate to email or call me directly.

detail_description:
Wellington Surf Lesson offer super fun group classes for both beginner through to intermediate level students and cater for students of all ages, from kids as young as 7 years old surfing with their parents through to adults of all ages.
Lessons are progressive so we recommend students take 2-3 beginner lessons alongside some practise rentals then 2-3 intermediate classes.
You can buy singular lessons, or for an even better deal, you can buy a Package Deals! and receive multiple lessons at a discount rate (For individual surfers only).
Once you've got your surfing to where it needs to be, you can book a FREE Consultation with one of our instructors on the best equipment to buy based on your current surfing ability and goals.
Beginners Classes (Option 1) - Beginner classes will focus on all the important fundamentals you should know before hitting the water by yourself E.g. beach safety, body positioning, basic pop up techniques, catching waves in the white water and more. After taking a few classes we highly recommend students do some practise rentals to practise by them selves.
Intermediate Classes (Option 2) - Intermediate classes will focus on riding unbroken waves, how to get through the waves properly, correct positioning to catch unbroken waves, how to turn and ride across the wave, advance pop up techniques and much more! These classes are suitable for students who have taken at least 2-3 beginner classes, had some practise by them selves and are feeling confident with their pop up in white water.
The lessons are progressive so we recommend students take the following lesson plan:
x3 beginner lessons alongside some practise rentals
x3 intermediate classes alongside some practise rentals
Private lessons with our expert instructors to fine tune your surfing further
For discounts on multiple surf lessons - please see Surf Lesson Packages (For individual surfers only)
Need some individual help during the classes?
If you need some individual help during our group classes, don't hesitate to chat with just one of the team at the start of the lesson about your current surfing experience and what you feel you need help with. We will then give you some individual help during the class to fine tune your surfing.
The group lessons are a mixed class of adults and kids so you can surf with your kids! Or if you prefer, a private group lesson or birthday party can be arranged just for the kids. All kids are provided with the right surfboard and wetsuit to get them having the most fun and learning quicker.

Notifications on your phone 2-3 days prior to when the surf is best and we are running surf classes & rentals.

Chat with a supportive group of like minded surfers who are also learning to surf

detail_description:
Explore remote and rarely visited wilderness
Amazing wilderness days with challenges, rewards and remote, dramatic landscapes.
Fly across World Heritage coastlines and mountain ranges to land deep in Southwest Tasmania – explore the wilderness waterways of Bathurst Harbour and Port Davey by sea kayak – paddle through changing landscapes from campsite to campsite – these are the attractions and challenges of our 8-Day Sea Kayaking Expedition.
Bathurst Harbour and Port Davey, in Tasmania’s Wilderness World Heritage Area, offer a combination of sheltered wilderness harbours, rugged ocean coastlines, remote islands and wild rivers. There are no roads and no settlements. Discover spectacular destinations in the best way possible – by water, at paddling pace.
Our guides know this pristine wilderness intimately – all the sheltered bays and open beaches, the peaks and islands, every hidden corner and comfortable campsite. After a spectacular flight to the remote airstrip at Melaleuca, your days will be spent exploring one of Tasmania’s most remote and beautiful coastlines, paddling through perfect reflections in the tannin-stained waters, beneath mountains that rise from the shore and calling in to sandy beaches.
This trip has a flexible itinerary with time for optional short walks or relaxing on the beach. Your nights will be spent in remote and hidden campsites. Every night you'll enjoy delicious food with a glass of wine.
Extensive kayaking experience is not necessary, but it is important to have a sound level of fitness, be comfortable with wilderness camping and, most of all, have a sense of adventure.
The adventure begins...
The journey begins at Cambridge Airport near Hobart with a 40-50 minute scenic flight. Our pilot decides whether to fly along the remote beaches of the South Coast, or over the wild Eastern Arthur Ranges before landing on the gravel strip at Melaleuca.
Our first night is spent here, giving us all time to immerse ourselves in the relaxed pace of the Southwest Tasmanian wilderness. After setting up camp we will provide an orientation of the sea kayaks. There will also be time to explore Melaleuca, including the Deny King Museum, Needwonee Aboriginal Interpretative Walk, historic tin mining areas and looking out for the endangered Orange-bellied Parrots who breed here over summer.
The first evening your guides will, over a convivial glass of wine, discuss itinerary options for the expedition after careful assessment of the weather conditions. We’re kayaking in a remote wilderness area and there are plenty of options for outstanding paddling destinations.
An example itinerary is available for download from our website!

detail_description:
Explore remote and rarely visited wilderness
An unforgettable expedition with challenges, rewards and remote landscapes.
This is the ultimate multi-day sea kayaking destination and has been named as the “most magnificent paddling destination in Australia” and “one of the world’s 10 epic sea kayak paddles”.
Bathurst Harbour and Port Davey, in Tasmania’s Wilderness World Heritage Area, offers a combination of sheltered wilderness harbours, remote islands and wild rivers. There are no roads and no settlements. Discover spectacular destinations in the best way possible - by water, at paddling pace.
Our guides know this pristine wilderness intimately – all the sheltered bays and open beaches, the peaks and islands, every hidden corner and comfortable campsite. After a spectacular flight to the remote airstrip at Melaleuca your days will be spent exploring one of Tasmania’s most remote and beautiful coastlines, paddling through perfect reflections in the tannin-stained waters, beneath mountains that rise from the shore and stopping in at sandy beaches.
Extensive kayaking experience is not necessary, but it is important to have a sound level of fitness, be comfortable with wilderness camping and, most of all, have a sense of adventure.
The adventure begins...
The journey begins at Cambridge Airport near Hobart with a 40-50 minute scenic flight. Our pilot decides whether to fly along the remote beaches of the South Coast, or over the wild Eastern Arthur Ranges before landing on the gravel strip at Melaleuca.
Our first night is spent here, giving us all time to immerse ourselves in the relaxed pace of the Southwest Tasmanian wilderness. After setting up camp we will provide an orientation of the sea kayaks. There will also be time to explore Melaleuca, including the Deny King Museum, Needwonee Aboriginal Interpretative Walk, historic tin mining areas and looking out for the endangered Orange-bellied Parrots who breed here over summer.
The first evening your guides will, over a convivial glass of wine, discuss itinerary options for the expedition after careful assessment of the weather conditions. We’re kayaking in a remote wilderness area and there are plenty of options for outstanding paddling destinations.
An example itinerary is available for download at the top right of this page.

detail_description:
Have you ever wanted to explore the amazing Ningaloo Reef?
This full day experience will take you on a adventure exploring the spectacular diving and snorkelling locations on the world heritage listed Ningaloo Reef.
You will have the unique opportunity to snorkel with manta rays, observe humpback whales as they migrate along our coast and SCUBA dive or snorkel at one of our favourite locations.
The tour meets at 8am and returns around 3pm. We start the day by checking you in at our shop (Shop 8, Coral Bay Arcade) where we will provide you with your equipment that you need for the day. From there we will travel to the jetty on our buses to begin the tour.
This tour includes a snorkel or dive on the incredible Ningaloo Reef where you have the chance to see a variety of tropical fish, possibly turtles, sharks and beautiful coral structures.
From here, we will head into the next bay area and send out spotter plane in search for manta rays. If we are successful in our search, then you would have the opportunity to snorkel with them.
Next we will cruise the bay in search of other marine animals while the crew prepare lunch. Following lunch, we will head outside the reef in search of humpback whales to view as they migrate and frolic their way along our coastline. Then it's time to head back to the jetty and finish the day back at the shop.
Our dive sites are beautiful coral reefs that have a varied depth of 4m to 12m, with the average depth being at 6-9m. As Ningaloo Reef is a fringing reef system, it is quite shallow all around but filled with spectacular coral structures and marine life. All of our dives are guided with a maximum group size of 8, although typically we have smaller groups.
Our dives are 45-50 minutes long and average visibility in Coral Bay is 10-15m but can vary depending on conditions. The water temperature varies from 20C up to 26C in the summer months and we provide full length 5mm wetsuits for our divers.

Departing Sydney’s iconic Central Railway Station at 7am you will be guided past some of Sydney’s best landmarks. Our local guides will provide informative facts about Hyde Park, NSW Parliament House and the Origins of old Sydney town, Australia’s first convict settlement. As you depart the Sydney CBD you will be stunned by views of the Sydney Harbour Bridge, the Sydney Opera House and the world’s most beautiful harbour, the one and only Sydney Harbour. Now it’s time to sit back and relax as we travel north along the M1 highway into the rugged Hawkesbury River region, a true bushland wilderness and one of Australia’s great rivers only 1 hour from the Sydney CDB. Leaving the mighty Hawkesbury region we stop briefly at what
the locals refer to as ‘The Twin Servo’s’ for coffee and a comfort stop. As we leave the M1 we are now in the Port Stephens local government area and the lands of
the traditional indigenous Worimi people. Next, we arrive at the Stockton Bight sand dunes, a coastal desert 32kms long and largest mobile sand dune system in the Southern Hemisphere. Stockton Bight will take your breath away. Here you will be warmly greeted by our friendly 4WD drivers and guides from Port Stephens 4WD Tours, who will help you onto their 19 seater 4WD red coaches for the 2km drive to “The Dunes”. It can be a little bit bumpy on the track to the Dunes as we navigate the ‘Woopdie Doos’, a series corrugated sand berms. Ok, now it’s time for Sandboarding. Your sandboarding guide will give you safety instructions and tips on techniques on how to sandboard successfully. Sandboarding is suitable for toddlers to grandparents and very safe. Sandboarding is referred to as ‘soft adventure’ however it is hard core family fun. So now it’s time to shake off that sand to go the tranquil coastal village of Nelson Bay, the heart of Port Stephens and home to Delbora Marina departure point for the your Dolphin Discovery Cruise. Before your cruise there is plenty of time to enjoy your lunch at the many waterside cafes or simply walk around sightseeing and taking in the seaside vibe. 
 Ok now it’s time to board your boat to see a marine wonderland with Moonshadow TQC Cruises, the largest dolphin cruise company in NSW. Port Stephens is home to 160 bottle nose dolphins, one of the most beautiful marine mammals on the planet. At times the dolphins love to surf the bow waves of Moonshadow’s boats and if you’re lucky they may give you a wink of their eye or you can just wink at them. There is heaps of other wildlife to see on the cruise from pelicans, sea eagles and even the odd seal. You will experience 90 minutes of cruising the blue blue waters of Port Stephens with expert commentary provided by Moonshadow’s experienced skippers. In the warmer months you can even take a plunge in the boom net at the rear of the boat but make sure you have a change of clothes. Take plenty of photos to capture these magic moments. You tired yet? It’s now time head south back to Sydney. But before we leave Port Stephens there is one last stop at B-Farm aka Murrays Brewery for a spot of wine tasting. B Farm has several exquisite wines for you to sample. They also have a stunning gift shop for you to buy the perfect gift for that special someone back home. All Aboard! Time to head back to the big smoke. So put your seat belt, press recline on your seat because it’s time for some shut eye on our trip back Sydney. So as the bus pulls back into Central Railway I’m sure you will say “that was One Perfect Day”. See you on the next our tour to the Blue Mountains if you haven’t already been. Now that’s a whole another story.

detail_description:
Download The App / Free Surf Lesson Notifications!
Our classes run every day surf is up and by downloading the Wellington Surf Lessons App you can receive notifications on your phone 2-3 days prior to when we are running classes. This is important as lessons are surf/weather dependant which means we may not have all our lesson times available on the calendar until a few days prior.
Wellington Surf Lesson offer super fun group classes for both beginner through to intermediate level students and cater for students of all ages, from kids as young as 7 years old surfing with their parents through to adults of all ages.
Lessons are progressive so we recommend students take 2-3 beginner lessons alongside some practise rentals then 2-3 intermediate classes.
See Package Deals!
Once you've got your surfing to where it needs to be, you can book a FREE Consultation with one of our instructors on the best equipment to buy based on your current surfing ability and goals.
Beginners Classes (Option 1) - Beginner classes will focus on all the important fundamentals you should know before hitting the water by yourself E.g. beach safety, body positioning, basic pop up techniques, catching waves in the white water and more. After taking a few classes we highly recommend students do some practise rentals to practise by them selves.
Intermediate Classes (Option 2) - Intermediate classes will focus on riding unbroken waves, how to get through the waves properly, correct positioning to catch unbroken waves, how to turn and ride across the wave, advance pop up techniques and much more! These classes are suitable for students who have taken at least 2-3 beginner classes, had some practise by them selves and are feeling confident with their pop up in white water.
The lessons are progressive so we recommend students take the following lesson plan:
x3 beginner lessons alongside some practise rentals
x3 intermediate classes alongside some practise rentals
Private lessons with our expert instructors to fine tune your surfing further

product_headline: Age 14+ • Multi-day Course • Enjoy a unique Catamaran Sailing Course
detail_description: Join the working crew aboard the 45ft catamaran Queimarla for an expedition-style 3 or 5 day course along Western Australia’s stunning coast. You’ll stand watches, steer, set sails, study weather, night-sail and take part in onboard living tasks while exploring remote islands, snorkelling, fishing and swimming. The course focuses on practical seamanship and safety, and successful participants earn internationally recognised IYT certificates to help them charter yachts worldwide. The atmosphere balances intensive training with time for adventure and camaraderie.
detail_booking_notes:
This course has been designed around an expedition along the Western Australian Coast where you will be part of a working crew, participating in all the skills you need to become a competent yachts person.
You will be trained to take over command of the yacht and by the end of the course should be able to handle the vessel safely and competently.
You will be studying an IYT sailing course and graduate with an internationally recognized certificate that will allow you to charter yachts around the world.
We will also fit in plenty of adventure including swimming, snorkelling, fishing, exploring and friendship.

Check our website to learn more about our sailing catamaran Queimarla (https://www.adventuresailing.com.au/catamaran-queimarla). She is a 45ft high performance sailing machine which is fully certified by AMSA (Australian Maritime Safety Authority)
Your captain/instructor Captain Paul (https://www.adventuresailing.com.au/the-team) is a fully qualified professional skipper (Master 45m) with over 35 years sailing experience. Few people know the coast as well as him. You can rest assured that you will be in safe hands on a very sea worthy vessel!

There are 3 courses that can be completed during a 5-day course. The one you study will depend on your experience and your training needs.
Option 1. International Crew Certificates (3 day summer trips): This course has NO prerequisites.
Minimum age 16.
This course is often chosen if folks require less training, therefore allowing more time for relaxing and enjoying the environment. (Less work more play)
This is a good introductory level, covering all the skills required to sail a large catamaran safely & competently.
More information on this course HERE (https://www.iytworld.com/courses/international-crew-training/)
Option 2. International Flotilla Skipper (5 day winter trips): You must hold a Marine Radio licence before the issue of this certificate. (This can be done on board during your course.)
Minimum age 16 years old.
This is a high-level training course with the aim of skilling you to be able to take command of a vessel up to 24m.

detail_what_not_to_bring: Baby wipes (these are the worst marine toilet blockers, and a blocked toilet is no fun for anyone) There will be plenty of opportunities to swim and wash.
detail_faqs:
Q: What qualifications can we get? A: We can offer you, at the successful passing of the exam, 3 qualifications at the end of this course. International Yacht Training, International bareboat skippers’ qualification.
International certificate of competency http://www.iytworld.com
Short range operators’ certificate of proficiency. (VHF radio Licence)
Q: Is there any online training available prior to joining Queimarla? A: We will provide you with a comprehensive “e course” that you can work through in the comfort of your own home prior to sailing with us.
You will also receive an “e copy” of the IYT textbook for your course.
We will also send you a series of links to online u tube clips that we think are knowledgeable and worth watching.
Q: What is your rough weather contingency plan? A: We place your safety above all other considerations.
Queimarla is a remarkable sea boat that has successfully sailed around the world. She is strong, safe and is fully approved by AMSA. We do not take undue risk; however, we do not hide from a little rough weather. This is your opportunity to stretch your envelope of comfort whilst having a lifelong professional sailor onboard with you.
Saying this we can fly home from the Abrolhos Islands if caught out there by extreme weather.
Q: Can we fish onboard? A: This is predominately a sailing trip, but we certainly tow a lure when able and have a fish at anchor. We do not bring fish home; we eat what we catch onboard. You must make sure you have a current WA Recreational Fishing license (https://www.fish.wa.gov.au/Fishing-and-Aquaculture/Recreational-Fishing/Pages/Recreational-Fishing-Licences.aspx) if you wish to spear fish, dive for crays or fish.
Q: Can we surf? A: We have no insurance for surfing.
Q: What about Diving? A: We would be crazy not to enjoy this incredible environment into which we are sailing. Yes, to snorkelling, yes to insurance, yes to we have gear onboard.
Q: What gear is onboard? A: All safety gear including life jackets & harnesses.
All bedding.
All Food and cooking equipment.
Fridge & Freezer.
Sunscreen.
Snorkelling gear
SUP board.
3.75m dinghy.
Basic fishing gear.
2 x SUP boards & paddles.
All training resources and equipment.
Blue tooth speaker.
Manual deck shower only
Salt water soap.
Q: Do we need to study? A: We get 3 different sorts of people onboard: Those that want the awesome experience, those that want to be able to sail a charter boat and need the qualifications and those that want to sail their own boats and adventures.
Which are you? The last two groups should do some pre-study as provided. This will deepen your learning. The first group can mix another piña colada and observe!
Q: Do I have to get the certificates? A: IYT charge $150 per certificate. You need them if chartering, they may reduce your insurance premium or make insurance easier to get and they look great in the pool room, but the choice is yours.
Q: Is there a hot shower? A: We spend a great deal of effort keeping water out of the boat, so there is no shower below decks. We do have a saltwater deck shower, saltwater soap available and a freshwater rinse down on deck. We try to swim every day and so far, we have had no complaints about our smell.
Please DO NOT bring baby wipes or body wipes. These things are an environmental disaster and the most prevalent blockers of marine toilets ever invented. They should be illegal.
Swimming in the blue ocean is a perfect way to stay clean and fresh. We will have biodegradable salt water soap that works a treat.
Q: What is the food like? A: I really like food. Lots of delicious fresh food. You will eat well and be part of the crew preparing these delicious meals. This can get a little competitive and result in some spectacular outcomes. You won’t be disappointed.
Q: How do we get to the boat? A: We mostly sail from Fremantle, Busselton, and Port Denison (Dongara). Travel to the boat is your responsibility. Some folk drive, some catch the Trans West bus. (Cheap and efficient) We have no secure parking available in Dongara. However, we have never had an issue. Yet.
Q: Coffee and Tea? A: We will have a selection of teas available on board, and fresh coffee beans. We have a hand crank coffee grinder, plungers and an Aeropress. It's a coveted job grinding the morning brew whilst standing up on deck staring at the water!

product_headline: Party with the Animals!
detail_description:
A special hosted Birthday Party at Urimbirra Wildlife Park will be sure to create lasting memories.
You can set up in our undercover or picnic areas, before the Park opens - while we take your guests on a fantastic adventure - a private meet and greet with the Koalas, feeding our noisy Rainbow Lorikeets and then on to a fun activity trail around the park interacting with our friendly animals and playing some games along the way!
A special "Party with the Animals" tshirt is available as an optional extra, for the Birthday Person - or the whole group! Minimum booking 6 children and 1 adult.
Sundays 9.30am start. Session is 2hours duration.
detail_booking_notes:
The session starts at 9.30am (before the Park opens at 10am) Mandy will greet you and give you access to set up in our Barbecue/Picnic area. Please ask the guests to arrive by 9.20am so we are ready to enter the Park at 9.30am. Any late comers will need to wait outside the Park (with their parent/guardian) until Mandy can go back and collect them.

Only Booked in participants will be allowed access before 10am.

Unbooked guests (parents/family) will need to pay upon entry at 10am.

The Birthday program is fairly flexible and is tailored to each group -It will include meeting, interacting and handfeeding our wide range of animals - from chickens, guinea pigs, sheep,and alpacas to quokkas, emus, koalas and kangaroos. and a very special feeding session with our very friendly rainbow lorikeets! As well as some animal related games and other fun activities.

Photos taken during the session will be available via our private Facebook Group - Urimbirra Programs. These could also feature on our social media pages - please let us know if you wish this NOT to occur.

We will arrive back to the Barbecue area at about 11.30 - and the children usually have built up an appetite! The Hosted part of the Program finishes at 11.30 - but you are more than welcome to stay on, have some lunch and go back out into the Park for another walk if you like. Children must be supervised by an adult. Please remember to be quiet and respectful around our animals - so that all will have an enjoyable time!

Don't leave any food unattended - our Kangaroos and peacocks have been known to be quite resourceful!

Parents will need to pick up their Children at your designated time. Please ask your guests parents to wait in the car park area when picking up their child There is an area to the right of the Entrance door - marked by a traffic cone- that allows space for them to gather safely - as the area inside the shop can become congested.

Parents can not enter the park to pick up their children

We would also appreciate the area being left neat and tidy - with any rubbish placed in the bins provided.

detail_description:
Experience the excitement of Boxing Day on Sydney Harbour aboard the Vagabond Cruises!
This Boxing Day, join us aboard our flagship, the MV Vagabond Spirit or our classic, timber MV Vagabond Princess and experience the excitement that is the start of the Rolex Sydney to Hobart Yacht Race with great food, fantastic service and electric atmosphere on spectacular Sydney Harbour.
Get up close to all the action whilst you dig into a delicious seafood and carvery lunch served to your table and enjoy live harbour commentary from your captain. Indulge in a selection of tempting desserts, coffee and tea and enter to win one of our lucky door prizes. Grab a cold drink at the bar and take advantage of our outdoor viewing decks as the yachts race for first place out of Sydney Heads and commence their 628 nautical mile journey to Hobart.
Over the past 75 years, the Rolex Sydney to Hobart Yacht Race has become an icon of Australia's summer sport, watched by millions all over the world and attracting people in the thousands to Sydney Harbour and its forshores on Boxing Day every year. With a range of tickets for adults, children, concessions and families, Vagabond Cruises invites you and the whole clan along to share in the tradition, innovation and excitement that is Boxing Day on spectacular Sydney Harbour.

detail_description:
Comfortable bush camping, great dining, fantastic service and wildlife encounters!
Our most popular trip. Using top quality equipment and accredited, qualified guides, this trip covers 40 to 55 kilometres of wildlife rich river, downstream from Katherine and away from the often crowded Nitmiluk National Park (Katherine Gorge). Fed by springs and soaks throughout the long ‘Dry Season’, the river below the Gorge, winds through rocky banks, paperbark forests, small rapids and pandanus channels. Comfortable bush camping, great dining, fantastic service and wildlife encounters – it all adds up to being a unique experience. A trip you will never forget.
We use a range of ‘Scupper Pro’ sit-on-top kayaks or 2 person canoes, (mainly for adult/child or couple pairing). The sit on tops are self draining, comfortable and very stable. The canoes are 4.5m open style polypropelene suited for touring. Many of our guests have never paddled before. Our fully qualified and accredited guides ensure that this is not a problem.
We are totally self sufficient giving us the luxury of being selective with our campsites and resting points along the river. There’s plenty of time to relax, swim, fish, bird watch, encounter wildlife and appreciate the scenery. We regularly access these sites with group sizes of 2-8, ensuring that we have minimal impact on the environment.
Typically, a 3 day trip can cover up to 50km of river. Paddling down stream, there is minimal portaging of equipment. Tours operate during the ‘TOP END’ dry season, May to September. The temperature ranges from 24 C to 39 C, but the nights from June to August can be cool, dropping to 8 degrees Celsius.
We are fully self-sustained while on tour, giving us the ability to stop and set camp, wherever we wish.
Exclusive to us and well equipped.
We bring out our rubbish; bury human waste 100m from water and burn toilet paper in the fire.
Always a surprise for the nature enthusiasts! All hearty home style fresh food. Dinners and breakfasts are cooked on an open fire
Lunches are ‘sandwich’ or ‘wrap’ style with cold meat and salad
A good old ‘Billy of Tea’ is available at lunch
Tea, Coffee and Hot chocolate are available at camp
The guide will do the washing up (unless you really want to help)

detail_itinerary:
Day 1 - You will be met at your Katherine accommodation between 7-7:30am (0700-0730). You will then be transferred in a 4WD vehicle to Gecko premises, where you will pack your personal effects required for the tour into waterproof bags. You will be fitted with Personal Flotation Devices (PFD) a requirement, to be worn whilst on the river. 
You will then be transferred to the Katherine River in a 4WD vehicle, sometimes over un-made roads and tracks. A safety brief and paddling instructions for kayaking and canoeing will be given before entering the water. At a relaxing rate, there will be stops along the river for a morning break, lunch, swim and time to view the diverse river environment, bird and wildlife. Approximately 4pm (1600) you will step ashore for an overnight remote camping experience (no set campsites). There will be time to relax; fish or read all whilst your guide prepares the evening meal. After a campfire meal, enjoyed with your favourite bottle of wine or spirit, sleep in a bed-roll (swag) under a blanket of stars. 
Day 2 - Wake to a dawn chorus in the brisk morning air. There is time for an early morning swim. After a hearty cooked breakfast, we pack-up camp and continue paddling down-stream. As we get further from immediate civilisation, the feel of remoteness sets in. The river continues to change from shady paperbark forests to lush pandanus channels, through open sections, surrounded by the river woods and over some small sparkling rapids which are fun and easy to negotiate. At the end of this satisfying day, you will find yourself in a bit of a routine and will have camp set-up quickly. Leaving yourself enough time to explore, relax, chat , check-out some animal tracks or just ‘find yourself’. 
Day 3 - After a sumptuous breakfast, we will pack up camp for the last time (you will now know where everything goes), we will return to the kayaks for one last relaxing day. You will be ‘tuned in’ to all the sights and sounds around you and will find yourself exhilarated by every experience, enjoy it while the moment lasts. At approximately 2:30pm (14:30) you will be picked up from the river and transferred in a 4WD back to Gecko premises to collect your belongings. You will then be transferred to your Katherine accommodation or bus terminal as per prior arrangements made. Tour end 5:30pm approximately.
