product_headline: $3,995 : 10 DAY + 9 NIGHT ADVENTURE (special 20% offer on now)
detail_description:
A fantastic opportunity to experience the Jatbula Trail and this remote and significant Savanna River of the ‘Top End’!
This Tour starts and ends in Darwin. A fantastic opportunity to experience the Jatbula Trail and this remote and significant Savanna River of the ‘Top End’ in the Katherine Region 9 Day Jatbula and Katherine River Discovery Tour’-Waterfalls, Rivers, Wildlife, and Aboriginal Rock-art sites.
Trekking – part 1
On the famous 'Jatbula Trail', 5 days Bushwalking through the remote stone country of the Jawoyn Peoples ‘Nitmiluk National Park’, along a traditional (Aboriginal) 'Message Stick' trail, which passes by Rock-art sites from the Katherine River to Edith Falls in Nitmiluk National Park
Kayaking – part 2
Using top quality equipment and qualified, accredited guides, this trip covers up to 50 kilometres of intimate river. Fed by springs and soaks year round, the river winds through rocky banks, paperbark forests, small sparkling rapids and pandanus channels. Wildlife encounters, comfortable ‘swag style’ camping, great dining, fantastic service, – it all adds up to being a unique experience. A trip you may never forget.
Tonight we camp nearby Nitmiluk National Park at our basic ‘but private’ bush camp, providing dinner and time to make sure that all your equipment is in working order before heading out on the trail.
Hiking into Northern Rock hole for Morning Tea allows time to adjust backpacks and hiking boots before they get too uncomfortable. Take a rest in the shade, drink some cool water and then continue onto camp at Biddlecombe Cascades where there will be time for a relaxing soak in some of the scenic and shaded rock pools.
After starting early – always good to get going on sunup – we continue on our way to Edith Falls. Today we will see the first of our Rock Art paintings, sheltered by an amazing rock formation; we will spend Morning Tea, again resting our backs and feet before moving onto camp at Crystal Falls. Crystal Creek is a great place to get out and stretch the body in the huge waterhole right beside the camp.
Another early start gets us to the Crystal Falls Lookout first thing for a sunrise, then we move onto the Amphitheatre for Morning Tea where we can leave our packs behind for 40 mins and descend into the cool monsoon forest to explore for more Rock Art, or maybe just sit in the shade and enjoy the serenity. Camp tonight is at the top of 17 Mile Falls, a walk to the bottom can be arranged, or you can just relax at the top of the falls in one of the cool and scenic pools.
Setting off at sunrise will give us time to get to the Edith River Crossing for a late Morning Tea/Early Lunch. Again a great place to take off the backpack and let the feet relax for a while. After our break we arrive at camp for the evening, a place called Sandy Billabong. Here you can swim or spa, a great place for bird watching in the afternoon, and the pool provides amazing reflection shots as the afternoon sky changes colour.
You will be back in time to unpack and repack then return to our private campground again (or you can choose to stay at a Motel (at own cost).
You will then be transferred to Gecko premises, where you will pack your personal effects required for the tour into waterproof bags. You will be fitted with Personal Flotation Devices (PFD) a requirement, to be worn whilst on the river.
You will then be transferred to the Katherine River in a 4WD vehicle, sometimes over un-made roads and tracks. A safety brief and paddling instructions for kayaking and canoeing will be given before entering the water. At a relaxing rate, there will be stops along the river for a morning break, lunch, swim and time to view the diverse river environment, bird and wildlife.
There will be time to relax; fish or read all whilst your guide prepares the evening meal. After a campfire meal, enjoyed with your favourite bottle of wine or spirit, sleep in a bed-roll (swag) under a blanket of stars.
Wake to a dawn chorus in the brisk morning air. There is time for an early morning swim. After a hearty cooked breakfast, we pack-up camp and continue paddling down-stream. As we get further from immediate civilisation, the feel of remoteness sets in. The river continues to change from shady paperbark forests to lush pandanus channels, through open sections, surrounded by the river woods and over some small sparkling rapids which are fun and easy to negotiate.
At the end of this satisfying day, you will find yourself in a bit of a routine and will have camp set-up quickly. Leaving yourself enough time to explore, relax, chat , check-out some animal tracks or just ‘find yourself’.
We will return to the kayaks for one last relaxing day. You will be ‘tuned in’ to all the sights and sounds around you and will find yourself exhilarated by every experience, enjoy it while the moment lasts.
You will then be transferred to your Katherine accommodation as per prior arrangements made.
We will transfer you to the Katherine Visitor Centre where you can have a refreshment. The centre is across the road from the transit centre, you can walk across to board your return bus back to Darwin.
Meals and Accommodation: 1 night Motel, 1 night Private Bush-Camp, and 6 nights remote bush-camping, that is, no facilities (except our own self sustaining equipment), camped under the stars at secluded riverside camps.
Evening meals, if you choose to book in a Katherine Motel are not provided, so that you may have your choice of where and when, you want to eat.
The Canoes/Kayaks
We use a range of ‘Scupper Pro’ sit-on-top kayaks or 2 person canoes, (mainly for adult/child or couple pairing). The sit on tops are self draining, comfortable and very stable. The canoes are 4.5m open style polypropelene suited for touring. Many of our guests have never paddled before. Our fully qualified and accredited guides ensure that this is not a problem.
Where We Stop
We are totally self sufficient giving us the luxury of being selective with our campsites and resting points along the river. There’s plenty of time to relax, swim, fish, bird watch, encounter wildlife and appreciate the scenery. We regularly access these sites with group sizes of 2-8, ensuring that we have minimal impact on the environment.
The Jatbula Trail is located within the boundaries of Nitmiluk National Park, following the Seventeen Mile Valley from Nitmiluk Gorge to Edith Falls. The local Flora and Fauna is prolific and the scenery is varied and beautiful. The Katherine River, Seventeen Mile Creek and the Edith River flow all year round and during the long drty-season, become the only water sources for all manner of wildlife. The Katherine Region is a terrific place to visit and base your Northern Territory experience from. We are close to The Kimberley, Gregory National Park, Elsey National Park, Manyallaluk, Kakadu Heritage Area and of course, right on our doorstep, is the magnificent Katherine/Flora/Daly River System.
Where We Stop
We are totally self sufficient giving us the luxury of being selective with our resting points, campsites however are designated due to the status of the National Park. There’s plenty of time to relax, swim, bird watch, encounter wildlife and appreciate the scenery. We regularly access these sites with group sizes of 2-8, ensuring that we have minimal impact on the environment. On the trail we are sharing sites with other hikers, numbers on the trail are generally small allowing groups to spread out and have their own area.
Tour Accommodation
We are fully self-sustained while on the trail. While hiking we stop at designated camping sites. If not providing your own equipment, You are provided with:
The Campsites
Fixed campsites on the jatbula Trail and on river they are exclusive to us and well equipped.
We bring out our rubbish; bury human waste 100m from water and burn toilet paper in the fire.
While we are on the hiking tour we forgo chairs and tables along with grills and camp ovens. We cook with small fuel burning stoves allowing us to have hot meals and hot drinks throughout the tour.
The Meals
Breakfasts consist of cereals/porridge/oatmeal
Dinners are typical light weight meals cooked on a fuel stove
Lunches are ‘sandwich’ or ‘wrap’ style (normally crisp breads)
Tea, Coffee and Hot chocolate are available at camp
The guide will do the washing up (unless you really want to help)
We recommend that you pack lightly and limit the space required. A packing list will be provided for you. For your personal gear we can provide:
A 65-75 litre backpack, (ruck sack), or you may wish to use your own. You will only need minimal clothing – you can rinse items out daily. Keep things as light and small as possible to compensate for food & water, a headlamp or torch (spare batteries) and personal first aid kit.

detail_itinerary:
Day 1 - 7:00AM pick-up from Darwin. We stop for a leg stretch (and coffee) enroute. You will arrive in Katherine in time to take an optional boat cruise in the magnificent Nitmiluk Gorge.
Day 2 - Hiking approx 8.2kms.
We leave our camp at 7 am approximately, where you will be transferred to Nitmiluk National Park and the 5 day walking trail, here you will catch a boat across to the mouth of the Seventeen Mile Creek where your trail begins.
Day 3 - Hiking approx 11.3kms.
Day 4 – Hiking approx 10.1kms.
Day 5 – Hiking approx 18kms.
Day 6 – Hiking 15kms.
One more early start will get us through some long grass, across a couple of creeks and through a bog all in time to have lunch at Sweetwater Pool. This is another amazing place to have a rest and contemplate why we do what we do! After leaving here it is but a mere 5kms more to Edith Falls where we can take the scenic lookout walk back to the kiosk where a cold drink and an ice cream will be waiting for us. We will be picked up at 3:00PM and head back to Katherine,
Day 7 – You will be met at your Katherine accommodation between 7-7:30am (0700-0730).
Approximately 4pm (1600) you will step ashore for an overnight remote camping experience (no set campsites).
Day 8 – Wake to a dawn chorus in the brisk morning air.
Day 9 - After a sumptuous breakfast, we will pack up camp for the last time (you will now know where everything goes)
At approximately 2:30pm (14:30) you will be picked up from the river and transferred in a 4WD back to Gecko premises to collect your belongings. Tour end 5:30pm approximately.
Day 10 - We will transfer you to the Katherine Visitor Centre where you can have a refreshment.

detail_description:
Join WAM on our epic 5 day Great Alpine & Lakes Adventure in the Victorian Alps & Gippsland Lakes.
From Skiing & Snowboarding Mount Hotham, Australia’s highest alpine village, snowshoeing to eco villages for dinner, driving the iconic Great Alpine Road, kayaking the Gippsland Lakes, bathing in the Metung Hot Springs with lake vistas, whale watching cruise at Wilsons Prom, and tasting fantastic produce along the way with a small group of likeminded legends.
The Great Alpine Road stretches from the Australian Alps to the Gippsland lakes and this trip is all about enjoying the best of the great outdoors during the cooler months amongst some of the most breathtaking scenery found anywhere in Australia.
detail_booking_notes:
Thanks for choosing this Great Alpine & Lakes winter adventure with WAM! We can't wait for you to join us on a spectacular journey into the Victorian Alps and Gippsland Lakes.

As one of Australia's only certified tour operator B-Corps, just by booking with us, you have done a lot of good for the planet, congratulations! (read on for more details of how)

Before we do so, please take a minute to read some important information about the trip:

For our Great Alpine & Lakes Adventure, we require a minimum of 5 people for the trip to run. If the trip does not reach minimum numbers, we will inform you at least 60 days prior to the trip and you will be provided with a full refund of what you have paid.
The balance of the trip is due 60 days before departure.
You’ll start receiving emails as we get closer to the date with information about the trip, what to bring etc.
Once you have the date confirmed, if you need to cancel, we require a minimum 60 days notice to provide a refund (less your deposit)

Pick up Location:
We will have 3 pick-up locations on the day of departure.
Mornington Peninsula
Frankston
Melbourne CBD
We will provide further details on these closer to the date.

Premium Service:
To maximise your comfort we provide you with an eco-pack for the trip which includes products from Australian businesses that directly support the environment. This includes a reusable water bottle, keep-cup, reef-safe sunscreen, sunscreen and a towel. You simply hand these back at the end of your experience. Its a bit like a pack you may get on a first class flight or a luxury hotel, except ours is good for the planet!

Now for the deep and meaningful:
By booking an adventure with us you have directly helped make a long-term positive environmental and social impact by:

Donating a portion of everything booking to Zoos Victoria to support the Mountain Pygmy Possum (and other endangered species), these little guys were thought to be extinct until being discovered in a loft in Hotham in the 1960's. Critically endangered, Mountain Pygmy Possums are Australia's only hibernating marsupial so will be sleeping while we are on the slopes above, knowing we have supported the conservation of this very special species.
Planting native trees on the Mornington Peninsula with MP Koalas to capture carbon emissions, protect our climate, enhance soil and water quality, and restore habitat for native wildlife.
Regenerate reefs and native kelp locally with The Nature Conservancy, providing marine habitat, filtering seawater, removing nitrogen and phosphate, and preventing used shell from entering landfill.
Support female education with The Stars Foundation which empowers and supports Indigenous young women and girls to complete education and find work.
Protect and plant mangroves to protect our coastlines, wildlife and support blue carbon projects.

You'll find additional information relevant to your adventure on the Wild Adventures Melbourne website. Please check the website for exactly what items we recommend bringing with you on the day.

Green is our Gold Commitment:

As members of Australia's tourism industry, we believe a land as precious
as ours should be preserved for generations to come. As a visitor, we ask that you do the same. That’s why we’ve set some unwritten rules that have kept our backyard beautiful for thousands of years.

Passed down through story and practice, they’re how we walk gently, listen deeply, tread with care – and look out for each other along the way.

By following them throughout your visit, you too can care for Australia when you Come and say G’day.

Consider these principles a bit of local knowledge. A few fundamentals to help you respect this place and have an unforgettable stay in the process.

The Guiding Principles:
Celebrate Community: The best part of an Australian visit is the people you meet. Shop local, engage with communities, and you’ll leave with new mates aplenty.
Embrace Culture: Australia’s cultural diversity stretches from ancient songlines to city laneways. Immerse yourself in it all - honour First Nations cultures, embrace our diversity, and you’ll leave with new knowledge and new friends.
Preserve Place: In Australia you’ll find some of the most unspoilt landscapes on Earth. Help keep them that way by minimising your impact wherever you go.
Respect Wildlife: Australia has some of the most unique animals on the planet. Take as many photos as you like but remember to give them space and respect their homes.
Take Care: We look out for one another in Australia, but it’s important to take care of yourself too. Listen to the land, respect it, and always put safety first.

If you have any questions between now and your trip with us, please don't hesitate to email or call me directly.

product_duration: 3 Days Practical and around 10-hours on-line learning
detail_description:
Get your PADI Certificate here and sea a whole new world.
We are Jervis Bays ONLY 5 Star PADI Accredited Dive Centre.
PADI (Professional Association of Diving Instructors) is the world's largest, most recognized scuba training organization, offering globally accepted certifications, the highest education and safety standards, and over 6,200 Dive Centers worldwide.
75% of all divers worldwide have chosen PADI as their certification authority.
With us, it is On-Line Learning followed by Three Days of Face to Face Training, including Confined Water Pool Session, Shore Diving and a DOUBLE BOAT DIVE in JERVIS BAY all included for less than $250 a day.
SMALLER CLASSES MEANS BETTER LEARNING OUTCOMES
If you've always wanted to learn how to scuba dive, discover new adventures or simply see the wonderous world beneath the waves, this is where it starts. The PADI Open Water Diver course is the world's most popular scuba course and has introduced millions of people to the adventurous diving lifestyle. Our Open Water classes include boat diving and rental gear for no extra cost as well as small classes to maximise your learning time.
If you are comparing courses, make sure you check what is offered.
The PADI Open Water Diver course consists of the following:
Knowledge Development (online, home study or in a classroom) to understand basic principles of scuba diving,
Confined Water Day to learn basic scuba skills
If for any reason we cannot complete the Boat Dive on Day 3, and we have to move it to a shore dive, we will provide you with a Gift Certificate for a free boat dive for you at any time in the next 3 months.
You will receive a confirmation email, stating all the details for your course once you have booked in and paid. This does not necessarily confirm that the course will definately go ahead on the dates requested.
We will need to reach our minimum number (2 People) for the course to proceed.
Please feel free to contact us if you need to discuss anything.
detail_itinerary:
2 Shore Dives on Day 2 to build on your skills
2 Boat Dives on Day 3 to complete your learning
detail_booking_notes:
The Program:
1. PADI ELearning: Before starting your Practical sessions however you will need to complete your PADI E-Learning. You can do this from home in your spare time as it suits you. You will need to allow 8 to 10 hours to complete it all. It is made up of short videos and questions for you to answer.
2. The Practical:
DAY 1: Your Open Water program generally starts at the SHOP at the start time indicated. You will meet your instructor, go through some theory, learn about Gear set up and how to put together your Diving Kit, and then head out to the pool to complete the confined water, skill development session.
DAY 2: We will take you out shore diving. The exact timing of the day will be discussed with you on Day 1, but you will need to allow at most 6 hours for the shore dives.
DAY 3: Is the final day of the course, this day will focus on boat diving, you can expect to be spending around 5 hours out on the boat for the last 2 dives of the course.
We usually send the PADI E-Learning (the theory) out to you a few weeks before the course. We do need you to complete it before you can hit the ocean, but we don't want you to do it too soon or you will forget everything before starting the practical.
E-Learning is a great way to learn the theory as you can do it in your own time. Don't worry though, there will be plenty of time to go over things during the course, if you have any questions, keep notes and talk to your instuctor about them.
Keep an eye out on your personal email for anything from PADI as your E-Learning, liability forms and other information will be sent to you directly from them, you will also need to electronically complete a Medical Questionaire and download a photo for your PADI E-Card.
If you are having any issues, have any questions or just feel like going over some things at all, feel free to reach out to our instructor team, remember that we are here to help you with your training.

product_name: Sydney Odyssey: A Sydney Harbour Walking Tour
product_headline: For all ages | 3 hours | Avoid the tourists and see Sydney from an alternative angle
detail_description: Join historian and archaeologist Elliot Lindsay on a thrilling walk from Circular Quay to Woolloomooloo, uncovering 12,000 years of Sydney’s hidden waterfront history. Wander past the Opera House, Botanic Gardens, Farm Cove and Mrs Macquarie’s Chair as you hear astonishing tales of 20-foot sharks, convict gangs, sailor riots, opium smugglers, Indigenous heroes, pioneering women, unsolved murders and the fiery destruction of the Garden Palace. Discover secret burials, forgotten carvings, bizarre legends and crime scenes tucked behind Sydney’s most iconic landmarks. A fascinating journey through beauty, mystery and mayhem—brought to life with vintage “then and now” photographs.
detail_booking_notes:
We will all meet 10 minutes before the start time at Customs House Square, which is in front of Customs House, Circular Quay. The exact meeting place is the benches under the sun awnings facing Young Street. Marked with the red arrow in the image below.

You can easily walk here from anywhere in the city, catch a train to Circular Quay Station, catch a bus to Alfred Street (such as the 333), or take the light rail to Circular Quay (the final stop).

If you are late or lost, please call Elliot on 0431922619. Your guide will be wearing a purple shirt.

Please wear good walking shoes to walk about 5km (3.1 miles). Bring water bottles and snacks. Wet weather gear if light rain is forecast. A hat and sunblock are advised as we will be outside in the sun.

We will stop around halfway at a cafe/bar, and you are welcome to purchase a coffee (even an Aperol Spritz!). We will pass a souvenir store in the Botanic Gardens next to the first restroom break. Please let the guide know in advance if you wish to visit it.

The tour ends at the Old Fitzroy Hotel in Woolloomooloo.

##What Happens if I Need to Cancel?##

We understand that plans can change unexpectedly, which is why we offer a flexible cancellation policy. Because our groups are intentionally small, we ask that you contact us as early as possible so we can offer your place to others. Advance notice also allows us to adjust bookings with our partner venues, many of which reserve space exclusively for Murders Most Foul.

##Group Public Tours and Talks##

Free cancellations and date changes (pending availability) are permitted up to 24 hours before your scheduled tour or talk.

All cancellations or date-change requests must be made by email to elliot@murdersmostfoul.com
 at least 24 hours in advance.

No refunds are issued for cancellations made within 24 hours of the tour.

Once a tour has commenced, no refunds or rebookings are available.

##Wet Weather Policy##

We review weather conditions 24 hours before the tour to determine whether it can safely proceed.

Tours generally continue in light to moderate rain or wind.

Conditions beyond this—such as heavy rain, strong winds, or flood-risk conditions—will likely result in cancellation, as many of our locations lack safe shelter and can flood quickly.

If the tour is cancelled due to weather, you will receive an email offering the following options:

1. Rebook for another date

2. Convert your tickets to a gift card (valid for 3 years)

3. Request a refund

We also understand that some guests may be unable to walk in wet conditions due to health, mobility, or personal comfort reasons. If light rain is forecast and you prefer not to attend, you are welcome to choose one of the options above.

##Private Tours and Groups (10+ participants)##

Private tours and large-group bookings have different cancellation conditions. These will be provided at the time of booking or upon request.

product_headline: 2 Day Beginner Surf Program (5 -14yrs)
detail_description:
Beginner Surfing Program with all equipment!
Over two consecutive fun filled days, you learn all the key base skills for paddling correctly and getting to your feet and riding with a good technique. You also get a thorough rundown of surf safety, ocean awareness, and surfing rules. You will progress your surfing with a focus on catching more waves, getting to your feet efficiently, surfing with the correct stance, and riding waves consistently. You will now be more confident in the surf and improving well.
The more lessons you surf with us, the more surfing skills and knowledge you will have to get past that initial, frustrating beginner stage.
Our instructors are there to help you learn to surf and provide advice on all questions related to surfing. We hope that you’ll love surfing as much as we do. We'll get you up and riding in no time!
Roll up at the beach at your start time with your swimwear on.
Your coach will introduce themselves and gets you sorted with a wetsuit and board.
You will start with some beach-based technique and surf safety info. We are big on getting it right on the beach and getting you ready to hit the waves.
You then hit the surf in waist deep water and waves suitable for your ability.
Surf coaches will help get you up and riding by pushing you into a few waves, giving feedback on your technique, keeping an eye on your safety, encouraging you and maximising your fun.
Surfers will leave the water approximately 15-20mins prior to the end of the lesson.
A feedback session with goals for your next surf lesson is done before getting changed.

product_name: Blood & Sawdust: A Forgotten History of Killara, Gordon, Pymble and St Ives (1820 to 1930). History Talk.
product_headline: A history talk with a complimentary drink and nibbles in a historical venue.
detail_description:
When one thinks of suburbs like Killara, Gordon, Pymble and St Ives, found on Sydney's Upper North Shore, it is common to visualise beautiful houses, pretty gardens, flowering jacaranda trees, tennis courts and European cars.
However, long before golf, netball, and lawn bowls became the preferred pastimes, the region was notorious for blood sports, horse racing, violent blood feuds, frontier justice and murder!
Come on the ultimate evening of discovery with a glass of wine or beer and nibbles, at the historical Killara Golf Club. Listen to historian and archaeologist Elliot Lindsay tell the most incredible stories of long-forgotten events dating between 1820 and 1930. Illustrated with a presentation of stunning maps, illustrations and photographs.
The event will be held in the Killara Golf Club clubhouse—one of Australia's oldest golf clubs. Established in 1899, it is one of the few remaining relics from a quaint bygone era. The clubhouse building dates back to 1933 and exudes old-world charm. Very few non-members ever have the opportunity to experience and observe the splendid beauty of the historical institution.
A complimentary drink and nibbles with each ticket
Each ticket comes with one complimentary glass of house wine, beer or non-alcoholic beverage. There will also be charcuterie board nibbles served.
The club house plenty of parking. However, it is only a 13 minute walk from Killara Train Station.
detail_highlights:
Battles with bushrangers.
The Killara Green Gate murder mystery.
Bare-knuckle boxing and cock fighting tournaments.
Naval battles on the Lane Cove River.
When the Rocks Push challenged the Waterhouse boys to a duel.
Peter Jackson, the legendary black heavyweight boxer who was trained at the Green Gate Hotel and became one of the world's greatest.
The Gordon murder mystery.
The Murder of Police Sargent Hickey on Pymble Golf Course. The long-forgotten pubs and gambling houses.

detail_description:
Check out Sydney's multicultural Inner West, on Dave’s Sydney Food Tour - The Marrickville Munch! 
Our bite-seeing walking tour will take you through some of our neighbourhood’s most famous eats, plus a few surprises we wanna 'keep under the cloche'!
detail_itinerary:
We’ll start at an iconic family-run deli forwith a coffee (or an iced cafe crema) and tasting of the house-made cheeses along with Australian olives and meats (kangaroo salami. ..yum!).
Next, its another Sydney icon and our most famous Banh Mi (Vietnamese pork roll). We’ll wash down that deliciousness with a beer from a local brewery. We think a sour matches best, but you may be a hop head and need an IPA or possibly you are in love with the darkness of a porter. No judgement, all beer is good beer...even the non alc stuff.
Following the refreshment, we’ve got some Aussie classics from our mate’s bakery for you to ‘wrap your laughing gear around’ (that’s an old Aussie term for eating).
Once you’ve filled up on your Aussie ‘tucker’ (food) quota, we’ll drop by another small cheese producer for a snack before the sweet sweet finish!
The dessert finale to the Marrickville Munch is at our favourite 'serial chillers’ headquarters. We may get to see what they are up to through the factory windows while we ‘get stuck into’ their house made gelato and crazy chocolate creations.

product_headline: 2 Hour Guided Tour • Culturally Significant Battle Site and Replica Trenches
detail_description:
Exclusive for ECE, Primary, Intermediate & High School Only
Minimum Number of 25 students for any group Booking
The He Toi Tupu Education Tour is tailored to pre-school, primary, intermediate and secondary schools. This experience will take schools on a journey through one of New Zealand’s most significant Maaori earthwork fortifications of the 1860s.
The Rangiriri invasion by military forces is considered to be one of the bloodiest battles during the crown invasion of Waikato. This tour aligns with Aotearoa New Zealand's Histories and Te Takanga o te Waa and provides opportunities for teachers to engage in alternative methods to deliver their Histories curriculum. Through this experience, teachers, leaders and aakonga will gain a better understanding of a historical event that has impacted and shaped our present-day lives of Waikato and the Kiingitanga.
Walk through the world’s first Maaori replica earthwork trenches built to scale. Journey into the 19th century and learn about the Maaori spirit of resilience that led to the survival of Waikato and their ally tribes. Be moved by the narratives told by descendants of the men, women, and children who committed the ultimate act of selflessness. We survived annihilation and live to tell the stories.
He Toi Tupu Education Tour includes visiting historic sites of significance including Te Maataarae ki Rangiriri (old paa site & military redoubt), the remnants of the original Rangiriri Paa earthworks and the world's first Maaori replica earthwork trenches built to its original scale. You will learn of the local narratives about the atrocities of the Waikato invasion and the stories behind the carved Pou (carved posts) and Tomokanga (carved entrances) carved by Kingitanga Master Carvers. Aakonga will learn and play the exhilarating trench warfare game Ika Ngohi (the first to be slain in battle).

detail_description: Tuff Nutterz is a lively, family-friendly event centred on Australia’s biggest inflatable obstacle course, with climbing walls, slides, tunnels and other challenging features for kids and adults. We require all visitors who are participating in any of our activities to sign a waiver as, like with any high-intensity activity, it informs you of the risks involved. Agree to follow any rules or advice from our staff on site
Agree to make sure that any children you are responsible for abiding by our rules
Understand that you, and any children you are responsible for, participate at your own risk

detail_restrictions:
All participants MUST have a signed waiver before entry.

Under 5’s require an accompanying parent/carer at ALL TIMES.

Adults MUST remain within the premises for all minors.

No food, no shoes, no sharp objects (including keys), no glasses, no glass, no jewellery, no candy, no gum, no mobile phones, no pets, no smoking, no alcohol or drugs or being under the influence of alcohol/drugs/medication.

No running, please take your time, no rushing or rushing others.

Allow plenty of space for the person in front of you.

ALWAYS look up whilst climbing. Do not climb underneath someone climbing above you. People can slip and fall whilst climbing. Use straps while climbing and take one step at a time.

No climbing or hanging from outside walls.

Make sure the landing area is clear of all people before jumping or sliding. Jump ONE at a time.

The correct sliding position on the slides is to have arms crossed across your chest with feet and legs together.

If sliding with another DO NOT hold hands. Slide separately.

Do not slide down any area that has climbing handles attached.

No pushing or rough play.

Smaller children should always be given right of way.

No tumbling or flipping and no diving.

Tread carefully and show caution as the course is uneven and spongy.

The course is only for use during public opening hours when obstacle course staff are on duty.

Obstacle Course staff directions must always be followed.

No medical conditions (Heart conditions, pregnancy, etc).Maximum weight 100Kg.

You may hear a whistle or megaphone announcement meaning stop and listen, wait for instructions in case of an emergency.

Enter at your own risk

detail_description:
Spirit Junior Island Cruise – Discover the Best of the Gold Coast
4-Hour Scenic Adventure You’ll Never Forget
9:30am - 1:30pm (Boarding at 9:00am)
Join us aboard Spirit Junior for a stunning 4-hour island cruise through the Gold Coast’s most beautiful waterways and island destinations. This small-group adventure combines breathtaking views, island exploring, swimming, wildlife encounters, and a delicious Aussie lunch — all in one unforgettable experience.
Cruise the Gold Coast Skyline
Your journey begins with a relaxing cruise past the iconic Gold Coast skyline, where city meets sea. Sit back and take in the shimmering views as we make our way toward Wave Break Island, a local favourite for swimming only accessible by boat.
Swim & Explore Wave Break Island
We’ll drop anchor for an hour at Wave Break Island, the perfect spot to enjoy a refreshing swim in calm, crystal-clear waters. Relax on the beach or dive in for a splash — this island paradise is your playground.
Island Hop to Tipplers via Sovereign Island
Next, we’ll cruise through the exclusive waterways of Sovereign Island, home to some of the Gold Coast’s most luxurious homes. Enjoy the scenery as we make our way to the famous Tipplers Bar & Café on South Stradbroke Island, a local gem surrounded by natural beauty.
Bushwalk & Wildlife Adventure
From Tipplers, embark on a gentle 900m bushwalk through lush coastal forest to a secluded surfside beach. Here, you’ll enjoy panoramic views of the Coral Sea and the chance to spot native wildlife including wallabies, echidnas, dolphins, dugongs, rays, turtles, marine birds and — if you’re lucky — the rare golden wallaby.
Aussie Lunch at Tipplers Café
Your cruise includes a freshly prepared Aussie-style lunch at Tipplers Café, with your choice of Fish & Chips, Calamari and Chips, BLTC (Vegetarian Option Available).
Prefer something different?
You can upgrade to the following for an additional $18 on the day:
Nachos with Avocado and Mexican Beef (Vegetarian Option Available)
Herb Crusted Hoki, Chips, Salad and Aioli
Tropical Chicken Burger with Chips
Scenic Return Cruise
After lunch, we’ll enjoy a leisurely return journey through the Broadwater, soaking in the peaceful waterways and coastal charm that make the Gold Coast so unique.

detail_description:
Booking a fishing charter offers a unique and exciting experience, blending adventure with the tranquillity of being on the water
Research and Selection: Clients should carefully select a charter based on the type of fishing experience they desire, considering factors like location, type of fish targeted, boat size, and customer reviews.
Booking and Confirmation: Once a charter is selected, clients will book their trip, and receive a confirmation detailing the trip date, duration, departure time, and location.
Preparation: Clients will be informed of what to bring. This usually includes appropriate clothing, sun protection, and any personal fishing gear they prefer, however noting that adequate fishing gear is always supplied. We don’t supply food, however we have bottled water readily available.
Safety Briefing: Before departure, there will be a safety briefing. Clients will learn about the boat's safety equipment and procedures.
The Fishing Experience: Once underway, the captain will head to the fishing spots. Clients can expect guidance from the crew on using the equipment and techniques to catch the targeted species. Charters often provide all fishing gear, bait, and licences.
Support and Instruction: For beginners or those looking to improve, the crew will offer instruction and support, helping with baiting hooks, casting, and landing fish.
Relaxation and Enjoyment: In addition to fishing, clients can enjoy the beauty of the open water and, in many cases, wildlife sightings. It's not just about the catch but also the experience of being at sea.
Return and Dock: At the end of the fishing trip, the boat will return to the dock. Clients often have the opportunity to take pictures with their catch.
Fish Cleaning and Packaging: All catch will be cleaned for you by the captain and packaged up. We strongly recommend bringing your own esky with ice packs that can be left in the car to keep the catch cool on the ride home.
Flexibility: Fishing conditions vary, so clients should be open to changing fishing spots or techniques as advised by the captain.
Booking a fishing charter is an adventure that offers the thrill of the catch, the beauty of the sea, and an opportunity to learn from experienced fishermen. With the right preparation and an open mind, clients can expect an enjoyable and memorable experience.

The Fishing Experience: Once underway, the captain will head to the fishing spots. Clients can expect guidance from the crew on using the equipment and techniques to catch the targeted species. Charters often provide all fishing gear, bait, and licences.
Support and Instruction: For beginners or those looking to improve, the crew will offer instruction and support, helping with baiting hooks, casting, and landing fish.

Flexibility: Fishing conditions vary, so clients should be open to changing fishing spots or techniques as advised by the captain.

detail_description:
Paddle & Pancakes!
Indulge in a luxurious breakfast experience featuring Maddison's Cafe's famous Gourmet Pancakes, a true culinary delight that will elevate your morning. These fluffy, golden pancakes, made with the finest ingredients and served with an array of delectable toppings, are the perfect start to your day of adventure.

After breakfast, set off on a mesmerising kayaking journey down the tranquil waters of the Kangaroo River, guided by a professionally accredited Guide who will be with you every step of the way. As you glide through the pristine environment, keep an eye out for the unique wildlife that calls this river home, including platypus, wombats, wallabies, and echidnas.

The journey offers a seamless blend of serenity and excitement, from the calm stretches of mirror-like water to the thrill of navigating gentle Grade-1 rapids. Imagine the thrill of spotting an Azure Kingfisher darting by, hearing the melodious mimicry of a Superb Lyrebird, and feeling the awe as a White-Bellied Sea Eagle soars above.

Your adventure concludes with a convenient return to Kangaroo Valley, where you'll have the opportunity to explore the charming village and its delightful array of shops. This is not just an outdoor experience; it's a day of gourmet indulgence and natural wonder that you’ll remember long after your paddle has touched the water's edge.

Bookings include 1x 600ml Water per person and complimentary Dry-bag hire.

detail_highlights:
🏙️ Cruise the Gold Coast Skyline
Your journey begins with a relaxing cruise past the iconic Gold Coast skyline, where city meets sea. Sit back and take in the shimmering views as we make our way toward Wave Break Island, a local favourite for swimming only accessible by boat.
🌊 Swim & Explore Wave Break Island
We’ll drop anchor for an hour at Wave Break Island, the perfect spot to enjoy a refreshing swim in calm, crystal-clear waters. Relax on the beach or dive in for a splash — this island paradise is your playground.
🌅 Sunset Cruise
As the sun descends towards the horizon, embark on a cruise through the picturesque Gold Coast Broadwater. From stunning GC skyline views through to Sovereign Island - home of the Gold Coast's multi-million dollar mansions - this is an experience not to be missed!
🏝️ Island Hop to Tipplers via Sovereign Island
Next, we’ll cruise through the exclusive waterways of Sovereign Island, home to some of the Gold Coast’s most luxurious homes. Enjoy the scenery as we make our way to the famous Tipplers Bar & Café on South Stradbroke Island, a local gem surrounded by natural beauty.
🌿 Bushwalk & Wildlife Adventure
From Tipplers, embark on a gentle 900m bushwalk through lush coastal forest to a secluded surfside beach. Here, you’ll enjoy panoramic views of the Coral Sea and the chance to spot native wildlife including wallabies, echidnas, dolphins, dugongs, rays, turtles, marine birds and — if you’re lucky — the rare golden wallaby.
🍴 Aussie Lunch at Tipplers Café
Your cruise includes a freshly prepared Aussie-style lunch at Tipplers Café, with your choice of Fish & Chips, Calamari and Chips, BLTC (Vegetarian Option Available).
Prefer something different?
🚤 Scenic Return Cruise
After lunch, we’ll enjoy a leisurely return journey through the Broadwater, soaking in the peaceful waterways and coastal charm that make the Gold Coast so unique.

detail_description:
Add some excitement and thrill to your tour with this daring and adventurous tree-top challenge, with more than 100 challenges including 11 huge flying foxes and Tarzan swings, overlooking stunning rainforest views in the heart of Mount Tamborine!
After you’ve conquered the tree-tops challenge, celebrate your achievements with a wine tasting and a delicious two-course lunch. To make it a full-day experience, you have the option to add a second wine or liqueur tasting to your itinerary.

detail_booking_notes:
We look forward to hosting a fun day out full of adventure, nature & an indulgent lunch.
Your first stop for the day will be Thunderbird Park, where you'll kick-start the day with a 3 hour TreeTop challenge. The TreeTop Challenge at Tamborine Mountain is Australia’s largest High Ropes Adventure Park with more than 120 TreeTop Activities, including 10 flying foxes! These courses range from easy to extreme and traverse through 9 acres of amazing bushland and rainforest. The adventure park is designed for all fitness levels and ages (from 8 years and over).
Please wear appropriate closed shoes & have your phones in a zipped pocket (or stored away before you embark on your TreeTop Challenge).
After an adventure packed morning, it's time to reward yourself with an indulgent winery lunch at the top of Mt Tamborine. Here, we'll start with a delicious wine tasting, followed by a delectable two-course lunch.
If you have selected the full day itinerary, we will finish the day off with a second wine or liqueur tasting before making our way back to your drop-off point.
A confirmed itinerary will be sent to you, along with your pickup times, in a separate email.
If you have any questions in the lead up to your tour, please don't hesitate to reach out.

detail_description:
Come and take a walk through our Greytown Flower Farm. We've planted thousands of dahlias this year to show the relationship between Bees and Flowers and the pollination that occurs.
Last year they attracted hundreds of people to come and have a look through and enjoy, and this year we've gone bigger again to allow a truly magical experience.
We've got different packages available and would love to hear about any special requirements to make sure we can cater for you.
We'll be adding extra capacity in closer to the time pending bloom numbers and if you're needing to visit outside of our standard picking timings please do get in touch - these extra dates/times will be available for wedding packages only and a minimum number of blooms will be required.
detail_booking_notes:
We can't wait to share our flower farm with you through our Dahlia Field. There's a few health and safety notes that are good to share before you come so you can be prepared - we're a bee farm, there'll be bees here so if you're allergic it's great if you let us know when you arrive. It doesn't stop you coming - but it does mean we're a bit more prepared. Footwear is a must - we can't let you out in the field with nothing protecting your feet.

If you're an avid dahlia grower and are wanting to know the names of the dahlias in our field, please do ask - Karly loves to share and although doesn't know every single one, we've got the large majority of them named and ready to share.

One of the best parts of our experiences is being outside in our peaceful environment up close and personal with the bees, or simply wandering through the flower farm. Learn more about the Tiaki promise here - https://www.tiakinewzealand.com/en_NZ/about-tiaki/

If you're a local kiwi the next question is going to be - are you selling tubers? We sure are - make sure you're following us on social media so you don't miss the announcement in May as to when our pre-season sale will take place.

Finally, we can't wait to see you in the flower farm - don't forget to bring a bucket to take them home (don't worry we have them available for purchase if you don't have one).
detail_health_safety: Please remember you're coming primarily to a Honey Farm - there'll be bees. While we have very calm bees and minimal beehives on our farm, the bees are the reason we have the flower farm. If you've got an allergy to bees, please let us know on arrival so we can talk you through a few extra health and safety considerations. You're still very welcome to come and enjoy our flower patch and pick your own flowers.

Sometimes plans change if you can't make it anymore, let us know.

- 0-48 hours notice = 100% cancellation fee

Precis of Queensland cycling rules and safety:
RULES:
PATHWAYS:
Shared pathways:
Keep Left, ring bell to warn of passing pedestrians
Cyclists give way to people, slow down
Separate pathways:
Cyclists use the side of the pathway indicated by the sign
Bicycle only:
For bicycles only
You can use any speed
On-road bicycle lanes.:
You must follow all road rules
You are sharing the road with other vehicles
Keep as far left as possible
NO Bicycle zone:
You must dismount and walk your bike
DO NOT RIDE IN PUBLIC SQUARES, WALK YOUR BIKE.
RIDING:
Keep at two hands on handlebars unless giving signals.
Have one leg on each side of the seat.
Face forward.
To signal RIGHT-TURN, extend arm out horizontally with hand open, palm facing forward. To signal STOP, raise arm with elbow bent at right angle and hand up with palm facing forward.
One person per bike unless the bike is designed as a tandem bike.
Keep two meters from the back of a vehicle when following.
DO NOT ride into the path of a driver or pedestrian.
Keep left at all times.
Do not overtake another vehicle on the left if that vehicle is indicating and turning left.
Do not ride more than two abreast.
If riding beside another rider, ride no more than 1.5m apart.
For a more comprehensive list of rules go to https://www.qld.gov.au/transport/safety/rules/wheeled-devices/bicycle
IF YOU BREAK THE ROAD RULES YOU MAY BE FINED. THERE IS NO AGE LIMIT FOR BEING FINED.
SAFETY:
Wear your helmet and enclosed shoes
Cycle at appropriate speed.
Go slow when there are people about.
Ring the bell when approaching pedestrians, dogs, etc.
Keep left at all times.
Use appropriate lights and reflectors in low light level situations and at night.

product_headline: An insiders tour with a two-wheeled, architectural twist.
detail_description:
Regeneration and renewal of Sydney's inner-fringe. An insiders tour of Sydney with a two-wheeled, architectural twist.
All tours led by practising architects.
Nominated as one of the world’s top five architecture tours by The Sydney Morning Herald.
Nominated as one of the world’s top ten architecture tours by The Guardian UK.

Join us on an architectural exploration of the former working-class suburbs of Redfern, Surry Hills and Waterloo. Until recently, these suburbs were associated more with pestilence, poverty and crime than hipster cafe's and bars but over recent decades these neighbourhoods have undergone massive change with a steady influx of squatters, students, artists and other creative types creating a thriving scene. Sure enough, the money, the foodies and the architects soon followed!

Sticking to bike paths, back lanes and quiet streets you will experience Sydney at her rawest and her grooviest. Our route and conversation will be structured around a number of contemporary projects, contested sites and politically charged themes. You will discover projects large and small including back-lane renovations, houses, public and cultural buildings, contemporary landscapes and paradigm-bending infill and apartment developments. We will cross political, cultural and economic territory as we discuss the patterns driving change and reveal the new ideas shaping how we live in the private and public realms.

Taking centre stage will be a suite of inspiring projects by local heroes Neeson Murcutt, Collins + Turner, SJB, Angelo Candalepas, John James, Ian Moore, Raffaello Rosselli and Andy Macdonald.

This tour is no touristic join-the-dots. It's an exploration of a city by stealth that will reveal an altogether different Sydney to the one you may have imagined.

Prince Alfred Park & Pool (outside) 105 Chalmers St, Surry Hills. 5min walk from Central Station.

You will need your own bike. There are various bike-hire and bike share operators to choose from including Mobike and Lime Electric Bikes.
If you have a Gift Card, enter the code in the next window.
Please bring your ticket for scanning either printed or on your phone.
Please arrive at the meeting point 10 minutes prior to tour departure.
Tickets are transferrable and cancellable up to 48 hours before the event.
The route is as safe and quiet as possible, a combination of bicycle paths, pavements, laneways and back streets. However, you will still need to be a reasonably confident cyclist. Gloves are a great idea if its cold, and a sun visor or beanie will fit under your helmet. Sunscreen is also a great idea (don't forget the back of your neck and hands!). Rain coat provided in case of unexpected wet weather.

Email info@sydneyarchitecture.org

SAW is a member of Guiding Architects, the international network for high-quality architecture tours.

detail_restrictions:
Precis of Queensland cycling rules and safety:
RULES:
PATHWAYS:
Shared pathways:
Keep Left, ring bell to warn of passing pedestrians
Cyclists give way to people, slow down
Separate pathways:
Cyclists use the side of the pathway indicated by the sign
Bicycle only:
For bicycles only
You can use any speed
On-road bicycle lanes.:
You must follow all road rules
You are sharing the road with other vehicles
Keep as far left as possible
NO Bicycle zone:
You must dismount and walk your bike
DO NOT RIDE IN PUBLIC SQUARES, WALK YOUR BIKE.
RIDING:
Keep at two hands on handlebars unless giving signals.
Have one leg on each side of the seat.
Face forward.
To signal RIGHT-TURN, extend arm out horizontally with hand open, palm facing forward. To signal STOP, raise arm with elbow bent at right angle and hand up with palm facing forward.
One person per bike unless the bike is designed as a tandem bike.
Keep two meters from the back of a vehicle when following.
DO NOT ride into the path of a driver or pedestrian.
Keep left at all times.
Do not overtake another vehicle on the left if that vehicle is indicating and turning left.
Do not ride more than two abreast.
If riding beside another rider, ride no more than 1.5m apart.
For a more comprehensive list of rules go to https://www.qld.gov.au/transport/safety/rules/wheeled-devices/bicycle
IF YOU BREAK THE ROAD RULES YOU MAY BE FINED. THERE IS NO AGE LIMIT FOR BEING FINED.
SAFETY:
Wear your helmet and enclosed shoes
Cycle at appropriate speed.
Go slow when there are people about.
Ring the bell when approaching pedestrians, dogs, etc.
Keep left at all times.
Use appropriate lights and reflectors in low light level situations and at night.

detail_disclaimers:
Milford Sound Risk Disclosure: Visitors to Milford Sound should be aware of various natural hazards when going to Milford Sound.
Aotearoa New Zealand: Powerful natural forces have shaped Aotearoa New Zealand over millions of years. Earthquakes and volcanoes lifted these beautiful islands out of the Pacific Ocean. They have created the dramatic landscapes we enjoy today.
Natural hazards are part of life here. Around 20,000 earthquakes are recorded each year. Most are small and go unnoticed, but larger events can cause damage. Understanding the hazards and how to stay safe is an important part of planning your visit.
Piopiotahi Milford Sound: Dramatic and ever-changing, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is one of the world’s most spectacular and special environments. Its steep, glacier-carved mountains and deep fiord have been shaped by powerful geological forces over millions of years.
The area is exposed to risk from a range of natural hazards. These can occur at any time, and some can happen without warning. Of all the hazards, large earthquakes, landslides and tsunamis pose the greatest risk to people at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
It is extremely unlikely that one will happen during your visit, especially for a short stay. However, there is a risk and the longer you spend there, the higher it becomes. Once you are there, your safety options are limited and it is important you understand the risks, before you go.
Earthquakes at Piopiotahi Milford Sound: Like the rest of Aotearoa New Zealand, small earthquakes occur regularly in Fiordland. We don’t feel them and they don’t bother us. These small movements are a normal part of how the land works and do not pose a risk to people.
Sometimes, earthquakes in or near Fiordland are felt at Piopiotahi Milford Sound. They might shake objects on a shelf or rattle a window, but they do not cause major impacts or disrupt your visit.
Occasionally, a stronger earthquake can trigger avalanches, rockfall or landslides. These can cause debris to fall onto roads, jetties and tracks, and may disrupt your travel plans if you happen to be nearby.
Large earthquakes are rare, and extremely unlikely to happen during a short visit. But they will happen again.
The Alpine Fault runs almost the entire length of the South Island and crosses the entrance to Piopiotahi Milford Sound. It can generate earthquakes of magnitude 8 or greater, occurring on average every 300 years. There is a 75% chance of this happening in the next 50 years (find out more at af8.org.nz (https://af8.org.nz/)). An earthquake of this size would almost certainly affect the narrow waterway and surrounding area.
What to do in an earthquake: DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries from earthquakes happen when you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the ground/floor you are, the less likely you are to be injured.
Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
For more detailed information, please visit Emergency Management Southland (https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or AF8 (https://af8.org.nz/).

Milford Sound Risk Disclosure: Visitors to Milford Sound should be aware of various natural hazards when going to Milford Sound.
Aotearoa New Zealand: Powerful natural forces have shaped Aotearoa New Zealand over millions of years. Earthquakes and volcanoes lifted these beautiful islands out of the Pacific Ocean. They have created the dramatic landscapes we enjoy today.
Natural hazards are part of life here. Around 20,000 earthquakes are recorded each year. Most are small and go unnoticed, but larger events can cause damage. Understanding the hazards and how to stay safe is an important part of planning your visit.
Piopiotahi Milford Sound: Dramatic and ever-changing, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is one of the world’s most spectacular and special environments. Its steep, glacier-carved mountains and deep fiord have been shaped by powerful geological forces over millions of years.
The area is exposed to risk from a range of natural hazards. These can occur at any time, and some can happen without warning. Of all the hazards, large earthquakes, landslides and tsunamis pose the greatest risk to people at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
It is extremely unlikely that one will happen during your visit, especially for a short stay. However, there is a risk and the longer you spend there, the higher it becomes. Once you are there, your safety options are limited and it is important you understand the risks, before you go.
Earthquakes at Piopiotahi Milford Sound: Like the rest of Aotearoa New Zealand, small earthquakes occur regularly in Fiordland. We don’t feel them and they don’t bother us. These small movements are a normal part of how the land works and do not pose a risk to people.
Sometimes, earthquakes in or near Fiordland are felt at Piopiotahi Milford Sound. They might shake objects on a shelf or rattle a window, but they do not cause major impacts or disrupt your visit.
Occasionally, a stronger earthquake can trigger avalanches, rockfall or landslides. These can cause debris to fall onto roads, jetties and tracks, and may disrupt your travel plans if you happen to be nearby.
Large earthquakes are rare, and extremely unlikely to happen during a short visit. But they will happen again.
The Alpine Fault runs almost the entire length of the South Island and crosses the entrance to Piopiotahi Milford Sound. It can generate earthquakes of magnitude 8 or greater, occurring on average every 300 years. There is a 75% chance of this happening in the next 50 years (find out more at af8.org.nz) (https://af8.org.nz/). An earthquake of this size would almost certainly affect the narrow waterway and surrounding area.
What to do in an earthquake: DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries from earthquakes happen when you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the ground/floor you are, the less likely you are to be injured.
Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.
For more detailed information, please visit Emergency Management Southland (https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or AF8 (https://af8.org.nz/).

detail_description:
Welcome Aboard as we head to the Ultra Trail Jervis Bay 53km Start Line Send Off
We will be departing from Huskisson Wharf and heading straight out to Murrays Beach to view the start of the 53km race from the water. What a way to start the day!
Your Captain will keep Port Venture steady just offshore so that the competitors can wave and you can cheer them off as loudly as you can.
With the start and cheering complete we will head back at a leisurely pace and do our best to find some of the local wildlife.
Never fear, we will be back on the dock at 9.30am to ensure anyone crewing can get there with ease, even with a brekkie stop at a local cafe!
Jervis Bay has been a Marine Park for 20 years and is now one of the most unique and healthy eco-systems in Australia.
That’s why the crystal clear waters of Jervis Bay are home to over 100 Bottlenose Dolphins. This species is highly recognisable and known for its long snout and distinctive smile.
We often find pods of dolphins feeding around the reef systems, particularly Plantation Point and Callala.
The dolphins sometimes swim and race hundreds of metres to play on our bow.
Their friendly and active behaviour will make you fall in love the moment you lay eyes on them.
Being winter you also have the pleasure of entering the ‘Whale Highway’ – with any luck we will spot a couple of the majestic Humpback Whales playing between Point Perpendicular and Bowen Island on their Northern Migration upon our return to Huskisson.
Please note that cruise times may change due to tide issues for the vessel Port Venture.

detail_description:
For those wanting a more relaxed and immersive time on the Whanganui River.
Experience one of New Zealand’s Great Journeys on this unforgettable 4-Day Freedom Hire Canoe Journey through the heart of the Whanganui National Park — including 1 night free accommodation at our base in Owhango prior to departure.
Paddle deep into remote wilderness as you journey from Whakahoro to Pipiriki through towering native bush, dramatic river gorges, waterfalls, historic river settlements and culturally significant landscapes accessible only by water.
This self-guided canoe adventure allows you to travel at your own pace while reconnecting with nature, escaping the modern world, and experiencing the peaceful rhythm of the Whanganui River.
Your journey begins with complimentary overnight accommodation at our base in Owhango, giving you time to relax, prepare your gear and enjoy a stress-free departure the following morning.
After a full safety briefing and paddling instruction session, our shuttle will transport you to the river launch point at Whakahoro where your adventure begins.
Over 4 days and 3 nights, you will paddle through some of the most scenic and remote sections of the Whanganui River Journey. Choose from a variety of DOC campsites, huts, and private accommodation options along the way, allowing flexibility to tailor the experience to suit your group.
One of the major highlights of the journey is the iconic Bridge to Nowhere. At Mangapurua Landing, pull your canoe ashore and take the 40-minute walk through native bush to visit this historic remnant of a once-isolated farming settlement abandoned between the World Wars.
The Whanganui River is not simply a canoe trip — it is a journey through living cultural history. Te Awa Tupua (the Whanganui River) holds deep spiritual and historical significance and remains an important taonga (treasure) to local iwi and communities.
At the completion of your journey, our team will collect you from Pipiriki and return you to Owhango, allowing you to relax after your adventure and reflect on your time on the river.

Kayak To Cape Hauy, A Star Feature Of Tasmania’s Newest World-Class Hike - The Three Capes Track
Tasmania's (if not Australia's) most spectacular day sea kayaking tour
Get up-close and personal with the southern hemisphere’s highest sea cliffs and resident Australian fur seals.

The Great Alpine Road stretches from the Australian Alps to the Gippsland coastline and this trip is all about enjoying the best of the great outdoors amongst some of the most breathtaking scenery found anywhere in Australia.
detail_booking_notes:
As one of Australia's only certified tour operator B-Corps, just by booking with us, you have done a lot of good for the planet, congratulations! (read on for more details of how)

Before we do so, please take a minute to read some important information about the trip:

For our Great Alpine & Lakes Adventure, we require a minimum of 5 people for the trip to run. If the trip does not reach minimum numbers, we will inform you at least 60 days prior to the trip and you will be provided with a full refund of what you have paid.
The balance of the trip is due 60 days before departure.
You’ll start receiving emails as we get closer to the date with information about the trip, what to bring etc.
Once you have the date confirmed, if you need to cancel, we require a minimum 60 days notice to provide a refund (less your deposit)

Now for the deep and meaningful:
By booking an adventure with us you have directly helped make a long-term positive environmental and social impact by:

Donating a portion of everything booking to Zoos Victoria to support the Mountain Pygmy Possum (and other endangered species), these little guys were thought to be extinct until being discovered in a loft in Hotham in the 1960's. Critically endangered, Mountain Pygmy Possums are Australia's only hibernating marsupial so will be sleeping while we are on the slopes above, knowing we have supported the conservation of this very special species.
Planting native trees on the Mornington Peninsula with MP Koalas to capture carbon emissions, protect our climate, enhance soil and water quality, and restore habitat for native wildlife.
Regenerate reefs and native kelp locally with The Nature Conservancy, providing marine habitat, filtering seawater, removing nitrogen and phosphate, and preventing used shell from entering landfill.
Support female education with The Stars Foundation which empowers and supports Indigenous young women and girls to complete education and find work.
Protect and plant mangroves to protect our coastlines, wildlife and support blue carbon projects.

You'll find additional information relevant to your adventure on the Wild Adventures Melbourne website. Please check the website for exactly what items we recommend bringing with you on the day.

Green is our Gold Commitment:
As members of Australia’s tourism industry, we believe a land as precious
as ours should be preserved for generations to come. As a visitor, we ask that you do the same. That’s why we’ve set some unwritten rules that have kept our backyard beautiful for thousands of years.

Passed down through story and practice, they’re how we walk gently, listen deeply, tread with care – and look out for each other along the way.

By following them throughout your visit, you too can care for Australia when you Come and say G’day.

Consider these principles a bit of local knowledge. A few fundamentals to help you respect this place and have an unforgettable stay in the process.

The Guiding Principles:
Celebrate Community: The best part of an Australian visit is the people you meet.
Shop local, engage with communities, and you’ll leave with new mates aplenty.

Embrace Culture: Australia’s cultural diversity stretches from ancient songlines to city laneways. Immerse yourself in it all - honour First Nations cultures, embrace our diversity, and you’ll leave with new knowledge and new friends.

Preserve Place: In Australia you’ll find some of the most unspoilt landscapes on Earth. Help keep them that way by minimising your impact wherever you go.

Respect Wildlife: Australia has some of the most unique animals on the planet. Take as many photos as you like but remember to give them space and respect their homes.

Take Care: We look out for one another in Australia, but it’s important to take care of yourself too. Listen to the land, respect it, and always put safety first.

If you have any questions between now and your trip with us, please don't hesitate to email or call me directly.

detail_description:
Packraft Adventure Race Training – DAY COURSE
Designed and tailored for Adventure Race paddlers in packrafts that seek to ensure that they have the knowledge and skills to race safely and competently on any river system.
This is a compressed day course for advanced training:
Go beyond basic strokes to include techniques like ferry gliding, eddy hopping, and breaking in/out of currents efficiently to navigate complex river features.
Develop a deeper understanding of how water flows and interacts with the riverbed to make smarter, safer choices during a race.
Master advanced rescue skills, including assisted and self-rescue, throw-bagging, and swift water swimming, which are critical in dynamic race environments.
Learn to assess risks and develop processes for safe river running, including scouting unfamiliar sections, identifying emergency exit points, and carrying appropriate safety and first-aid gear.
Develop skills for guiding a team and making decisions under pressure, which is essential for success in team-based adventure races.
Understand how to use and maintain your packraft and associated gear, including carrying an emergency repair kit.
QUALIFIED GUIDES – LOCAL KNOWLEDGE
Whitewater paddling can be a fast paced, adrenaline pumping experience. So having the confidence and skills to be more agile and to adapt to the dynamic style of paddling that river rapids demand is important.
Exodus Adventures is based where the mighty Nymboida River and Boyd Rivers join force. We have over 35 years of local knowledge and whitewater experience and specialise in whitewater training.
Our whitewater guides are knowledgeable and very experienced and will ensure your day is both fun and safe.
Our guided training packages will give you the most diverse paddling conditions found anywhere in the world. Explore Australia’s longest-mapped whitewater canoe and kayak trail.
The Nymboida River is also reckoned as a premier river for whitewater and is regarded as one of the best paddling and rafting rivers in Australia. It is also the closest rafting river to Brisbane.
On the Nymboida River you will experience surging grade 1-3 rapids and exciting whitewater. Our whitewater tours will also guide you through deep tranquil pools where you experience the region’s best fauna and flora - you may even see a platypus!
The Boyd River is not to be missed. Thrilling grade 1-3 rapids and the best of the area’s wildlife – rock wallabies, water dragons, wombats, lyrebirds, and the golden, blue and red dragonflies. A photographers dream!
COME FOR THE WEEKEND - FREE CAMPING
Please feel free to camp on our beautiful Exodus Property free of charge for the weekend and to use the time to do your own land based training.
If you would like any land based training included please contact us to discuss.
Participants are encouraged to bring their own packraft.
This will allow you to practice and improve your paddling techniques and boat control using the actual boat you plan to use in the future, ensuring you develop relevant and specific skills for its intended use.
Please let us know if you are missing any gear so we can assist.
Choose your own date - please email us with your referred date via admin@exodusadventures.com.au

detail_description:
Book now and join our scenic train trip from Drysdale to Queenscliff and return!
Depart Drysdale Station at 10:30am, and sit back as the train works its way though the rugged Bellarine landscape on an unforgettable train journey to the seaside.
Arrival at Queenscliff will be at 11:15am, just in time to find lunch at one of the local eateries, and then explore all the fascinating history that Queenscliff has to offer.
The train will depart Queenscliff at 1:45pm for the journey back towards Drysdale.
detail_highlights:
Your adventure begins at your selected Station, where you’ll be greeted by our friendly volunteers in traditional heritage uniforms. Take some time to explore the station and view the beautifully restored train before boarding your carriage.

Once aboard, your train will set off on a 45–55 minute journey through the Bellarine countryside — passing rolling hills, trestle bridges, farmland, and forest, following the Swan Bay shoreline.

At Queenscliff, you’ll have around two hours to explore the seaside town. Enjoy lunch, browse the local shops, or take a walk along the beach before rejoining the train for the relaxing return trip to Drysdale.

detail_description: Independent walkers begin their Ngaro Track journey with a scenic boat transfer to Whitsunday Island, the gateway to this challenging 32km, 3-day hike. detail_important_info:

You must make your own arrangements to get to and from the start and end points of the Ngaro Track.

Arrive early for all departures and pick-ups — operators are often unable to wait due to tidal and safety constraints.
Understand that missing your scheduled transfer may result in needing to remain on the island overnight. Always carry extra food and water in case of delays.
Confirm all booking details directly with your chosen operator before travelling to ensure a smooth connection at both ends of the walk.

A National Park Camp Permit is required for all overnight stays.
Rangers patrol the islands regularly.
Book your permit here: Queensland Parks Booking
🔥 IMPORTANT RULES:
Open fires are NOT permitted on any Queensland National Park islands or beaches.
Glass items are NOT allowed on the vessel.
No beach trolleys – these are unsafe onboard and not permitted.
King swags incur extra charges and must be pre-approved. They may be refused if not declared, as the vessel has limited space.

https://www2.gbrmpa.gov.au/access/zoning/eye-on-the-reef-app

Small dome tent
Sleeping bags & mats
55L cooler or esky
Dry food container
Gas stove & utensils
Snorkel gear
Insect repellent / sunscreen (reef-safe preferred)

detail_description: Hop aboard our buggy and experience the true essence of an Australian working farm. As we drive through the beating heart of Windy Station, you'll get a genuine, behind-the-scenes look at everyday farm life and how it changes from season to season; the good, the bad and ugly. With stunning Australian landscapes as your backdrop, this immersive tour offers a unique opportunity to connect with the land and the hardworking farmers who bring it to life. detail_booking_notes:
We’re excited to have you join us and want to ensure you have a safe and enjoyable time on the water. Please take a moment to read the important information below regarding your booking:
Booking Times
Please arrive on time, as bookings are scheduled to ensure smooth and efficient service for all guests.
Collection and Return Point
Kayaks and paddleboards are collected and returned at the Penneshaw Penguin Centre. Kayak trolleys are available to assist with transporting equipment to the beach (approximately 20 metres away).
Clothing and Belongings
This is a water-based activity, so please dress appropriately for getting wet. A limited number of dry bags are available to borrow; however, you are welcome to bring your own if preferred.

Upon collection, our staff will provide a map and indicate areas where kayaking and paddleboarding are not permitted for safety reasons. Please follow all guidance provided.

detail_description:
Travel just 1.5 hours west of Sydney to experience nature on a grand scale in the UNESCO World Heritage–listed Blue Mountains. Famous for its towering sandstone cliffs, misty valleys, waterfalls, and lush eucalyptus forests, this iconic region has long been a favourite destination for both locals and visitors.
Upon arrival in the mountains, take in spectacular panoramic views from Echo Point, home to the legendary Three Sisters rock formation. Learn about the area’s rich Aboriginal heritage while enjoying sweeping views across the Jamison Valley.
Continue to Scenic World for an unforgettable experience, where your Unlimited Discovery Pass includes all three signature rides. Descend into the valley on the world’s steepest passenger railway, glide above the rainforest canopy on the cableway, and cross the valley floor on the Skyway with breathtaking views of Katoomba Falls and surrounding cliffs. Enjoy time to explore the sub-tropical rainforest boardwalks at your own pace.
Afterward, stop at Cahill’s Lookout for stunning views over the Megalong Valley, offering a quieter and more peaceful perspective of the Blue Mountains. The tour then continues to the charming village of Leura, where you’ll have free time to enjoy lunch (at your own expense), explore boutique shops, or relax in one of the local cafés.
This half-day experience offers the perfect balance of natural scenery, iconic attractions, and relaxed exploration before returning to Sydney in the afternoon.

detail_description:
For everyone who wants to get wet, this is a trip out into the Jervis Bay Marine Park. We will usually visit two of the bays' many dive site for an hour each, allowing everyone to explore either on or under the water.
This is a trip on a smaller dive boats in the Jervis Bay Marine Park. We cater for all people as best we can depending on conditions. You can be a snorkeler, experienced tech diver or anywhere in between on a general boat dive.
On return you can leave directly from the Boat or spend the rest of the day in the park itself there are a number of activities to do within the park, as well as some of the best beaches in the area.
Because of the shape of Jervis Bay, there are dive sites that are sheltered in all but the worst conditions. Average visibility is 10 – 15 meters, and most sites slope down from 5 meters to 30 - 40 meters so you can choose your depth depending on your experience.
We have over 65 Dive Sites with a wide variety of options.

The shark nursery
Sea caves and caverns
Governors Wall

Whales at the Bluff in winter

detail_description:
Embark on an unforgettable overnight journey through the wild beauty and rich culture of Tropical North Queensland. This carefully curated adventure takes you beyond the ordinary, deep into the heart of the Daintree Rainforest and out to the vibrant Great Barrier Reef.
Begin your experience at Mossman Gorge, where you’ll take part in a deeply meaningful cultural experience. Afterwards, enjoy lunch in the rainforest before travelling deeper into Cape Tribulation, where you'll spend the night surrounded by lush jungle and the soothing sounds of nature under the stars.
Day 2 -The next morning, step aboard a custom-built vessel for a half-day Great Barrier Reef adventure. Snorkel at a vibrant coral site teeming with marine life—colourful fish, giant clams, and perhaps even a curious turtle cruising by.
After your reef experience, relax and take in the views as you begin your return journey, wrapping up an immersive overnight escape that blends nature, culture and adventure into one seamless small-group experience.

detail_description:
Tried worm farming before and ended up unsure, overwhelmed, or wondering what went wrong?
This hands-on workshop will show you a simple, reliable way to turn everyday food waste into rich, living compost at home.
You'll learn how Bokashi fermentation uses beneficial microbes to transform kitchen scraps into powerful worm food. It's the missing step that allows you to process a wider range of household food waste — including many scraps that would normally cause problems in a standard worm farm.
Perfect for home gardeners, food growers, renters, balcony gardeners, and anyone wanting to keep food waste out of landfill, this workshop will show you how to close the loop at home with a system that actually works.
You don't need a big backyard to get started. Bokashi can be done in a small space, and if you don't yet have a worm farm, fermented Bokashi can be buried directly into garden soil where it continues breaking down into compost.
You'll leave with a clear blueprint for turning food waste into garden fertility, along with the confidence to set up a system that works for your home.

How beneficial microbes help transform food waste

How to set up and maintain a thriving worm farm
